before: Paste a SKILL.md. Your AI checks the name, trigger line, steps, hand-back shape and risky lines, then lists each problem with a fixed version.
after: A skill with a vague trigger line never gets picked up, and one with a loose step gives different results each time. You usually find out only after it has failed in front of someone.

before: Describe your project. Get the right rules and files loaded so your AI stays accurate through long sessions.
after: A short rules file and a tidy set of project files that tell your AI what you are building and how you work, so it stops guessing.

before: Describe your command-line tool. Get rules and a check so AI agents can run it safely with clean output.
after: Your command-line tool, reshaped so an AI agent can run it without breaking things. You get a clear rule set and a way to check each rule, so you know what is already safe and what still needs work.

before: Give it a vague job. Get a goal an AI agent can finish, with proof of done, limits and stop rules.
after: A vague job turned into a goal an AI agent can actually finish. The goal says what done looks like, what proof counts, what is off limits, and when the agent must stop and ask you.

before: Give it an AI agent and a test set. Get a loop that rewrites its prompts and skills until scores rise.
after: An AI agent that gets better on its own, because a loop keeps testing it and rewriting its instructions until scores go up. Each round changes one thing, and a change that makes results worse is rolled back.

before: Point it at your repo. Get a short, checked AGENTS.md with real commands and no guesses.
after: A short AGENTS.md for your code project where every command was checked and nothing was guessed. Your AI coding tool reads this file first, so a wrong line costs you on every task.

before: Say the job you want repeated. Get a bounded AI loop with checks, stop rules and handoffs.
after: A repeating job for an AI agent with clear checks, a point where it must stop, and a handoff to you when it is stuck.

before: Describe what your agent must remember. Get a memory design for short-term, long-term and graph storage.
after: A plan for what your AI agent remembers, where each memory is kept, and how it gets back into the conversation. Without memory, an agent forgets everything when the session ends.

before: Describe a repeatable job. Get a step-by-step procedure file for your AI, with firm rules and a format check.
after: A step-by-step procedure file that an AI agent follows the same way each time, for a job you repeat. It has inputs you can change, clear steps, and firm rules the agent cannot wave off.

before: Paste a rough request. Answer a few questions. Get one clear prompt to give an AI agent.
after: One clear prompt, ready to hand to an AI agent, written from your rough request. The skill writes the instruction. It never does the work the prompt describes.

before: Give it logs from an AI agent run. Get each success claim checked against real proof, with gaps marked.
after: A claim-by-claim check of whether an AI agent really did what it says it did. A confident "all done" is not proof, so each success claim is matched to records.

before: Describe your AI agent. Get a way to measure how well it works and compare changes.
after: A way to measure how well your AI agent works, so you can tell if a change made it better or worse. Agents answer differently each run and can reach a goal by several paths, so one pass or fail test is not enough.

before: Describe the jobs your agents do. Get a team of AI agents with roles, tasks and shared memory.
after: A team of AI agents, each with a role, a task and shared memory, ready to run as a group. One agent might research, another might write, and a third might check the draft.

before: Describe what your agent must do. Get tool definitions it can use well, with fewer and clearer tools.
after: Tool definitions your AI agent can pick and use correctly, with fewer tools and clearer ones. Most agent failures come from tools that overlap or describe themselves badly.

before: Give it your AI agent. Get a safe, authorized test plan and a report of where it can be tricked.
after: A safe, approved plan to find where your AI agent can be tricked, plus a report of what was found. It treats written permission as step one.

before: Describe your AI agent. Get a plan to trace its steps, costs and errors without logging private data.
after: A plan to see what your AI agent is doing: each step, how long it took, what it cost and where it failed. Nobody's private text gets stored.

before: Describe your AI agent. Get a test set, scoring rules and a release decision memo you can trust.
after: A test set, scoring rules and a release memo for your AI agent, built so a decision-maker can trust the result. It avoids cherry-picked demos.

before: Describe the job. Get a multi-agent design with handoffs, failure handling and cost limits.
after: A plan for splitting a big job across several AI agents, with clear handoffs, failure handling and a cost cap for each step. Many jobs do not need this.

before: Give it a subject. Get a worksheet that has students judge an AI answer on clarity, evidence and fairness.
after: A class worksheet set that teaches students to read an AI answer closely instead of trusting how smooth it sounds. It is built around six standards for judging claims: clear, accurate, precise, relevant, deep and broad.

before: After any AI explanation, you name one place it could be wrong, one thing to check and one source to try.
after: A three-question habit that turns any AI answer into a claim to test, not a fact to accept. After the AI explains something, the learner must say where it could be wrong, what they would check, and which source they would use.

before: Paste one or more AI answers. Get each claim checked against public sources, with links and a short verdict.
after: A list of the claims in an AI answer, each checked against current public sources, with links and a short verdict. It also compares answers from several AIs and shows where they agree, clash or leave out proof.

before: Say what good looks like. Get a scoring guide an AI can use to grade answers fairly, with bias checks.
after: A scoring guide that an AI judge can use to grade answers the same way each time, plus checks for the biases judges are known to have.

before: Describe your AI feature. Get a test plan with scores, human review and A/B checks to catch weak answers.
after: A plan to test whether your AI feature gives good answers, and to catch drops in quality before users do. It mixes quick computed scores, human review and live A/B tests, so no single method has to carry everything.

before: Describe the app you want. Get working code for a chatbot, question answerer or agent that uses tools.
after: Working code for a chatbot, a document question answerer, or an agent that uses tools, written with the LangChain library. It runs on your choice of AI provider, so you can swap one for another later.

before: Describe what your AI app must never do. Get rules that block jailbreaks, made-up facts and leaked personal details.
after: Safety rules for your AI app that block jailbreaks, made-up facts and leaked personal details before a reply goes out. You say what the app must never do, and the rules enforce it at run time.

before: Point it at your AI app. Get the weak spots found and layered defences added against hijacked instructions.
after: Your AI app checked for hijacked instructions and given layers of defence. Prompt injection happens when text from a user, web page or document tells the AI to ignore its real rules.

before: Describe what your AI agent does. Get clear rules for which actions need a person to approve and when to escalate.
after: Clear rules for which actions your AI agent may do alone, which need a person to approve, and who steps in when nobody answers. A yes-or-no pop-up is not real oversight, so the approval is tied to the exact action being taken.

before: Describe your AI product. Get a style guide for a chat-first screen with few controls and clear outcomes.
after: A style guide for an AI product where the main screen is a conversation, with few buttons and a clear result at the end. The guide is built so designers and engineers can use it directly.

before: Give it your tasks and how your team uses AI agents. Get time estimates with likely ranges you can plan on.
after: Time estimates for work done with AI agents, shown as a likely range you can plan on instead of one hopeful number. It works for a single task or a backlog of hundreds.

before: Give it a brand name. Get a score for where it is mentioned online. Collects data from websites.
after: A score for how often and where your brand is mentioned across the web, and which mentions matter for AI assistants. It collects data from websites, so expect it to browse public pages for you.

before: Describe an AI plan. Get an API vs fine-tune call, AI risk class under EU rules and cost break-even.
after: Describe an AI plan. Get an API vs fine-tune call, AI risk class under EU rules and cost break-even. Bring a description of your AI use case. Use the result to plan your next step.

before: Give it a page. Get each passage scored on how easily AI tools can quote it, with rewrites to try.
after: Every passage on your page scored for how easily an AI tool can lift it into an answer, with rewrites to try. Research found that AI picks passages that stand alone, answer a question up front and carry real facts.

before: Describe your AI app. Get where the tokens go and changes that cut the bill without hurting quality.
after: A clear view of where your AI app's tokens go, and a list of changes that cut the bill without hurting quality. The aim is often 40 to 80 percent less, and you measure first so you know which change worked.

before: Say which AI crawlers to allow. Get your robots.txt updated so AI assistants can read your catalog. Changes your live theme.
after: Your Shopify store's robots.txt updated so AI assistants such as ChatGPT, Claude and Perplexity can read your catalog. If the file blocks them or says nothing, people shopping through AI may never see you.

before: Say what data to pull from AI answers. Get code that returns checked, typed results instead of free text.
after: Code that pulls specific facts out of an AI's reply and hands back checked, typed data, not loose text. Your next step, like a database write or a screen, can then rely on the shape.

before: Name your business or industry. Get your exposure to AI on ten points and a 90-day plan to defend.
after: A score for how exposed your business is to AI, on ten points, and a 90-day plan to defend it. It finds where pressure from AI breaks your model first.

before: Give it a topic. Get a step-by-step way for students to check AI claims and citations before they trust them.
after: A class activity that teaches students to check an AI's claims and citations before they trust them. AI makes errors that old fact-check rules miss, because there is no author or funder to look up.

before: Paste the feedback your tool gives students. Get a check of its timing and wording, plus a better version.
after: A check of the feedback your AI tool gives students, with a better version written for you. Vague feedback such as "good effort" changes nothing.

before: Give it your store. Get an llms.txt guide to your brand, products and policies for AI assistants. Changes your live theme.
after: An llms.txt file for your Shopify store, a plain-text guide that tells AI assistants who you are, what you sell and where your key pages are.

before: Describe an AI use at work. Get risks, rules that apply and conditions to meet. Not legal advice.
after: Describe an AI use at work. Get risks, rules that apply and conditions to meet. Not legal advice. Bring the AI use you are assessing. Use the result to plan your next step.

before: Say which skill or instruction file you are writing. Get it written so your AI follows it well.
after: A guide to writing skills and instruction files so your AI follows them the same way each run. It applies to skills, AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md, and any document the AI is pointed to.

before: Give it your UI code. Get a 0 to 100 score, why it looks AI-made and a ranked fix list.
after: Your screen looks off and you cannot say why. This review finds the reason. It reads your UI code, scores it from 0 to 100 and points to the exact lines that make it look machine-made.

before: Describe how you run AI. Get gaps against ISO 42001 and a plan to close them.
after: A clear picture of where your AI governance falls short of ISO 42001, plus a 12 month audit plan to close the gaps. That standard covers how a company manages its AI systems.

before: Connect any memory tool. Get clear rules for when your AI recalls and saves decisions, so it stops repeating itself.
after: Your AI has a memory tool connected, yet it still asks the same questions and forgets what you decided last week. This skill gives it standing rules for when to look things up and when to write them down.

before: Give it a PyTorch or LiteRT model. Get C, C++ or CUDA code that runs it inside your app.
after: Turn a trained AI model into C, C++ or CUDA code that runs inside your own product or on hardware. The model stays the same.

before: Give it an AI-made product photo. Get a risk rating, eight checks and lines to add to your prompt before you retry.
after: Check an AI-made product photo before it reaches an ad. You get a risk rating of low, medium or high, a verdict on each of eight checks, and a call to run it, redo it or send it for a manual touch-up.

before: Give it a topic. Get rounds of questions students put to a chatbot, to see if it gives in or truly updates.
after: Rounds of questions your students can put to a chatbot, built to show whether it truly changes its answer or just gives in to pressure.

before: Name two or more subjects. Get lessons that show where AI is reliable and where it distorts, subject by subject.
after: A lesson sequence that shows students where AI answers can be trusted and where they bend the truth, one school subject at a time. A chatbot may do well on a biology process and badly on a historical judgement.

before: Give it your research code and results. Get a paper draft for a top AI conference, with citations checked.
after: A full first draft of a machine learning paper, written from your code, results and notes, and aimed at venues such as NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR and ACL.

before: Describe your AI system. Get risks mapped, measured and managed under the NIST AI framework, with a plan.
after: Your AI system's risks, laid out under the NIST AI Risk Management Framework, with owners and next steps. NIST is the US standards body, and the framework is voluntary, so this is a way to organise your thinking, not a compliance badge.

before: Give it a website. Get a score for how likely AI search is to cite it, plus fixes. Collects data from websites.
after: A score out of 100 for how likely ChatGPT, Perplexity, Claude and Google AI to cite your site, with fixes sorted by urgency. Pages built for AI answers can earn far more mentions, so this shows where you stand.

before: Give it a site. Get a score and fix list for Google AI Overviews, ChatGPT, Perplexity and more.
after: Each AI search tool picks its sources by its own rules, so a site that wins in one can be missing from another. Only about one domain in nine is cited by both ChatGPT and Google AI Overviews for the same question.

before: Give it your website. Get what blocks you in Google and AI answers, with fixes. Scrapes sites.
after: Find out what stops customers finding you in Google and in AI assistants, and get the actual files to fix it. The aim is to make your site easy to read and quote correctly.

before: Give it a page or topic. Get edits that help ChatGPT, Perplexity and Google AI answers cite you.
after: Edits to a page or topic that make AI search tools more likely to pull it into answers and name you as the source. The target is Google AI Overviews, ChatGPT, Perplexity and similar tools.

before: Give it your Shopify store link. Get a 6-point scorecard of what AI shopping tools can read. Scrapes sites.
after: Can an AI shopping assistant actually read your Shopify store? In about two minutes you get a six point scorecard with proof for each result, set against 99 other stores.

before: Run it on your store. Get a score for how easily AI shoppers find your products, plus the fix for each gap.
after: A readiness score for how easily AI shoppers can find, read and trust your products, with a fix for each gap. It reads straight from inside your Shopify admin, so it sees more than an outside scan can.

before: Point it at code that calls paid AI services. Get spending caps and loop limits added before a surprise bill.
after: Code that calls paid AI services can run up a huge bill. A loop that looks finite can repeat forever if a bug feeds it new work.

before: Point it at an AI app. Get prompt injection, jailbreak and tool abuse risks found, ranked and mapped to known attacks.
after: A ranked list of the ways someone could abuse your AI app, each tied to a known attack type. Test it before real users or attackers do.

before: Describe a messy planning problem. Get one clear decision, an AI fit check and a safe hand-off plan.
after: Turn a messy supply chain headache into one decision that your team can name, measure and safely hand to AI. It starts from a real event, such as a late shipment or a stockout, not from a technology wish.

before: Describe what a tool does. Get a clear, safe definition your AI can call without guessing.
after: A tool definition that your AI can call correctly the first time, with fewer wrong picks and invented inputs. The goal is to make the safe, intended call easier to choose than a risky one.

before: Describe what your AI needs to do. Get clear tool definitions it can call without guessing or failing silently.
after: Tools the model understands and uses correctly, instead of guessing, failing silently or burning tokens. Your AI never sees your code. It sees only the name, the schema and the description, so those are what get designed here.

before: Tell it how students use AI on a task. Get checkpoints that show whether they really understand the work.
after: Students who use AI can feel they understand a topic because the answer reads so smoothly. Checkpoints that expose the gap between what they think they know and what they can do turn that into a lesson.

before: Give it an AI tool's terms or addendum. Get data-training, liability and model-change risks flagged. A first check, not legal advice.
after: Spot the risky clauses in an AI vendor's contract before you sign. You get the key issues first, then a clause by clause review and suggested wording changes.

before: Give it a one-line video idea. Get a shot list, a ready prompt per shot and fixes for failed clips.
after: A shot list and one ready prompt per shot for your AI video, plus a plan to fix clips that came out wrong. Most failed clips break for dull reasons: two actions in one clip, no camera move, a changing subject, or a mood instead of an image.

before: Finish a task. Get an honest score on quality and effort, with the weak spots named.
after: An honest score for the work you just finished, not the usual 4 out of 5 for everything. It rates how hard the task was and how well it was done, then combines them with a fixed table.

before: Point it at a repo. Get a report on where outside text could reach an AI agent in your GitHub workflows.
after: Point it at a repo. Get a report on where outside text could reach an AI agent in your GitHub workflows. Bring the repo, or its workflow files. Use the result to plan your next step.

before: Describe how your team writes. Get what AI should draft, what people own, and rules that keep your voice.
after: A clear split of who does what when your team writes with AI. People own the voice, the facts and what gets published. AI does the research summaries, first drafts, edit suggestions and quality checks, always under a person's direction.

before: Give it code an AI wrote fast. Get the real risks that will hurt later, with the smallest fix for each.
after: Code that runs but feels fragile gets a plain risk review: what will hurt later, why, and the smallest fix for each. It looks at what rapid AI-assisted coding often leaves behind and ignores cosmetic nitpicks.

before: Paste a document. Get an honest estimate of whether AI wrote it, with the wording clues behind it.
after: Paste a document. Get an honest estimate of whether AI wrote it, with the wording clues behind it. Bring a document as a file, link or pasted text. Use the result to plan your next step.

before: Name a rival. Get a fair comparison or alternative page built to rank and convince buyers.
after: A comparison or alternative page for a named rival, written so it ranks for searches like "X alternative" and helps a buyer decide. It leads with fairness, because readers check claims and trust fades fast when you misstate a competitor.

before: Give it your brand and listings. Get checks for hijackers and fakes, plus complaint letters ready to send.
after: A set of checks and ready complaint templates to protect your Amazon brand from hijackers, fakes and sellers breaking your price rules. It works to risk levels, so you know what needs action in 24 hours and what only needs watching.

before: Tell it how you source and ship. Get the biggest cost bottlenecks and ways to cut them.
after: Find the biggest cost leaks in how you source and ship Amazon stock, and get ways to cut them. You just describe your situation in a sentence or two, and no account links or data feeds are needed.

before: Give it a product or category. Get Amazon sales rank, reviews and seller data in a report. Collects data from websites.
after: A research report on an Amazon product or category built from live data: search results, rankings, Best Sellers, New Releases, seller catalogues and reviews. Each point comes with the source link so you can check it.

before: Give it rival listings and reviews. Get their weak spots, your best selling points, and a ranked fix list.
after: A clear view of where rival Amazon listings fall short and what to say about your own product to win. Reviews are the source: complaints show gaps, and praise shows what buyers value.

before: Give it your product cost and price. Get fees, profit margin, break-even point and a price to charge.
after: Know what you really keep on each Amazon FBA sale before you buy stock. Enter your price and costs and get the full cost breakdown, profit margin, break-even point and a suggested price for the margin you want.

before: Tell it about your analysis. Get every assumption logged with its risk, so reviewers see what could change the answer.
after: Every analysis rests on choices that could change the answer. A log of them lets a reviewer see what you assumed, how sure you are, and what breaks if you are wrong.

before: Give it an analysis before you share it. Get a check of the method, the math and any bias.
after: Give it an analysis before you share it. Get a check of the method, the math and any bias. Bring the analysis as a report, file, query or description. Use the result to plan your next step.

before: Tell it how a data project went. Get what worked, what slipped, the causes and actions for next time.
after: A short written review after a data project that records what worked, what slipped and why, and who does what next time. Do it within a week, while the details are fresh.

before: Give it a brief and your data. Get ordered steps with time estimates and a list of risks.
after: A step by step plan for a data analysis, with time estimates and a list of what could go wrong, made before you touch any data.

before: Give it a vague request for data work. Get the right questions asked and a clear brief ready to hand over.
after: Give it a vague request for data work. Get the right questions asked and a clear brief ready to hand over. Bring the original request, however vague. Use the result to plan your next step.

before: Give it your finished analysis. Get a write-up with the question, data, method, results and steps to rerun it.
after: A finished analysis turned into a write-up that someone else can read, trust and rerun. It covers the question, the data, the method, the results and the steps to repeat it, so your future self will not have to guess.

before: Give it a stock ticker. Get how analyst profit and sales forecasts are changing and where they differ. Collects data from websites.
after: Before you buy or hold a stock, you can see whether analysts are getting more hopeful or more worried about it. Give a ticker and you get a plain read on profit and sales forecasts: the average, the high and low calls, and how far apart they sit.

before: Paste the complaint and your draft reply. Get promises, facts and tone checked, plus a repaired draft.
after: A reply to an upset customer can calm things down or make them worse. Paste the complaint and your draft, and you get a clear list of what works and what will backfire, plus a repaired version you can send.

before: Give it welfare readings from an animal study. Get one severity score over time and an early forecast.
after: Lab studies often track many welfare signs at once, like weight, temperature and activity. This skill folds them into one severity score for each animal on each day, so you can see who is struggling and who is likely to be next.

before: Answer a few questions about your product. Get a one-page site with 3D motion and scroll effects.
after: One self-contained web page for your product, with 3D motion, scroll effects and depth that follows the mouse. You can open it in a browser right away.

before: Give it a code change with motion. Get a table of fixes and a clear approve or block verdict.
after: A code change that touches motion gets a strict review and a clear verdict, Approve or Block, so nothing sluggish or jarring ships. The review comes as a table of findings, each with a suggested fix.

before: Point it at stuttering animations. Get each slow spot found and a small fix that smooths it.
after: Animations that stutter make a good product feel cheap. Point this skill at the troubled code and it finds each slow spot, explains the cause in one sentence, and gives a small fix.

before: Give it company facts. Get a one-page teaser that sells the business without naming it.
after: When you sell a company, you need to spark buyer interest without giving away whose it is. This skill writes a one-page anonymous teaser that sells the business and keeps the name hidden until a buyer signs an NDA.

before: Get two or three sharp follow-up questions after an answer, so you check the facts and the thinking.
after: After the AI gives you advice, a plan or a number, you get two or three sharp questions that help you check it before you act.

before: Name the frequency and goal. Get an antenna or array designed, with its pattern and fit checked.
after: Tell it the frequency and what the antenna must do, and you get a working design with its radiation pattern, impedance and fit checked. It can cover a single antenna, a circuit board antenna or a whole array.

before: Give it an antenna. Get a matching network and system model that connect it to your RF chain.
after: An antenna that does not match your radio wastes power and sends signal back. This skill builds the matching network and the system model that tie your antenna to the rest of your radio chain, so the signal actually gets out.

before: Name the service you need to reach. Get working code with sign-in, error handling and retries.
after: Working code that talks to an outside service, with sign-in, error handling and retries already in it. Name the service you want to reach and describe what you need from it, and you get a connector you can run.

before: Give it an API and its users. Get tests that catch breaking changes between the two before they ship.
after: Tests that catch the moment an API change would break the programs using it, before it reaches anyone. Give it the API and a list of who calls it, and you get a small test set that checks both sides.

before: Give it your API spec. Get a scorecard, flagged breaking changes and fixes for naming and errors.
after: A scorecard for your API design, with a list of breaking changes and fixes for naming, errors and structure. It works best before an API ships, or before you plan a second version.

before: Say what your code needs to offer. Get a clear, stable API or module design that is hard to misuse.
after: An interface for your code that is clear, stable and hard to misuse. Say what your code needs to offer, and you get a design for the routes, types or module boundaries, with the contract written down first.

before: Point it at your API. Get rate limiting added with Upstash, using the right window type for each route.
after: Your API gets a request limit that works across every server instance, so one bad actor cannot flood your login or sign-up routes. You get the code in place and a clear reason for each choice.

before: Name the API. Get safe code for waiting, retrying and backing off when it says slow down.
after: Code that handles an API saying slow down, without crashing your app or sending the same action twice. Name the API and you get a retry layer that is safe, bounded and easy to read.

before: Point it at your API routes. Get a check of sign-in, access rules and input, with fixes for each gap.
after: A check of your API routes from the moment a request arrives to the data it returns, with a fix for every gap it finds.

before: Describe your API or paste its code. Get a complete OpenAPI or Swagger spec ready for docs and SDKs.
after: A full, valid OpenAPI or Swagger file for your API, ready to feed your docs and client libraries. Describe the API in words, or paste your route code, and the file is written for you with no placeholders left.

before: Give it your Postman collection. Get a ready CI pipeline file that runs your API tests on every push.
after: A ready pipeline file that runs your API tests every time someone pushes code, so a broken endpoint is caught within minutes. You hand over your Postman collection and name your build tool.

before: Point it at your endpoints. Get integration and contract tests for each route, with fixtures.
after: Test files for every route in your API, covering sign-in, bad input, error codes and the edge cases people forget. Point it at your code and it finds the endpoints for you.

before: Give it an API spec. Get an MCP server in Python or TypeScript that lets your AI use that API.
after: An MCP server that lets your AI use a real API, built from the API's own spec instead of hand-written wrappers. Give it an OpenAPI file and you get a server in Python or TypeScript that exposes each action as a tool.

before: Describe the task to automate. Get an Apify Actor project with inputs, outputs and deploy steps. Needs a paid Apify account.
after: Describe the task to automate. Get an Apify Actor project with inputs, outputs and deploy steps. Needs a paid Apify account. Bring the task to automate. Use the result to plan your next step.

before: Give it an existing script or project. Get it ready to run as an Apify Actor.
after: Give it an existing script or project. Get it ready to run as an Apify Actor. Bring your existing code or project folder. Use the result to plan your next step.

before: Give it an Apify Actor. Get output schema files that show its results as a clear table. Needs a paid Apify account.
after: Give it an Apify Actor. Get output schema files that show its results as a clear table. Needs a paid Apify account. Bring the Actor project folder. Use the result to plan your next step.

before: Describe your shipped app. Get fixes for fit, flow, clarity and honest persuasion, step by step.
after: A shipped app that works but feels rough, turned into one that fits its job, flows without friction, reads clearly and persuades honestly. You get a step-by-step plan, not a one-off list.

before: Point it at your running app. Get sharp, high-resolution screenshots ready for Product Hunt, social or your site.
after: Sharp, high-resolution screenshots of your running app, ready for Product Hunt, social posts, a landing page or docs. You point it at your local or live app address and pick how many shots you need.

before: Describe your app. Get a retention plan with a habit loop, a better first run and one metric to watch.
after: People sign up for your app, then quietly drift away. This skill gives you a retention plan: a habit loop that brings people back, a better first run, and one number your team agrees to watch.

before: Give it your app listing. Get a scored audit and a rewritten title, keywords, description and screenshots plan.
after: A scored audit of your App Store or Google Play page, plus rewritten text that helps more people find it and install it. Share the link and it does the checking.

before: Point it at your app's code history. Get plain "What's New" notes users can read, based on real changes.
after: Plain "What's New" notes your users can read, built from what truly changed since your last release. No more guessing from memory or pasting raw commit text.

before: Point it at your app. Get hardcoded text found and a plan for translations, locale files and right-to-left support.
after: Your app, prepared for more than one language: hardcoded text found, translation files organised and right-to-left layouts planned. You get a clear route from one language to many.

before: Name your Expo app. Get crash rates, installs and update sizes for each published update.
after: A clear read on whether your latest Expo app update is healthy: crash rate, launches, unique users and bundle size, for each published update. You can answer is the new release crashing more than the last one in minutes.

before: Show it your iPhone, iPad or Mac app design. Get what to fix to match Apple's design rules.

before: Give it a product idea. Get one researched build document with stack, steps and tests an AI can build from.
after: One long document that an AI coding agent can build your product from, epic by epic, without stopping to guess. It starts from an idea that may be only two or three lines.

before: Describe how you ship. Get automatic checks and a deploy pipeline so bad changes never reach users.
after: Describe how you ship. Get automatic checks and a deploy pipeline so bad changes never reach users. Bring your language and tools. Use the result to plan your next step.

before: Point it at your project. Get a CI/CD pipeline file for your stack with test and deploy stages.
after: Point it at your project. Get a CI/CD pipeline file for your stack with test and deploy stages. Bring your project folder. Use the result to plan your next step.

before: Describe what you plan to build. Get the biggest risks on demand and switching, plus the smallest test to run first.
after: Find out if what you plan to build is worth building, before you write any code. You get the biggest risks named and the smallest test to try first.

before: Describe your customisable product. Get a plan with option rules, live pricing, checks and saving.
after: A plan for a build-your-own product tool that people finish, not abandon. It covers the choices to show, the rules between them, live pricing, checks and saving.

before: Give it orders and tracking numbers. Get them fulfilled in one batch, with customer alerts if you choose. Changes live orders.
after: Fulfil many open Shopify orders in one batch, adding tracking numbers and, if you choose, sending shipping emails. It changes live orders, so always preview first.

before: Pick products and a percent or amount. Get every price changed at once, within limits. Changes live prices, so preview first.
after: Change prices across a whole collection or tag in one go, within a floor and a ceiling you set. It edits live prices, so preview first.

before: Paste messy notes or an article. Get tidy nested bullets that are quick to scan and revise.
after: Paste messy notes or an article. Get tidy nested bullets that are quick to scan and revise. Bring text, notes or an article. Use the result to plan your next step.

before: Run it on your orders. Get the product pairs and triples people buy together, as ideas for bundles and cross-sells.
after: Find which products your customers already buy together, so your bundles and cross-sells start from real orders, not hunches. It only reads data and changes nothing.

before: Run it on your bundles. Get a check that every part is in stock, and how many bundles you can really sell.
after: Find bundles that look in stock on your storefront but cannot be shipped because one part ran out. It only reads data and changes nothing.

before: Say who buys from you. Get a plan for thought leadership and trust with slow, careful business buyers.
after: Say who buys from you. Get a plan for thought leadership and trust with slow, careful business buyers. Bring your product or service. Use the result to plan your next step.

before: Give it a business idea. Get the one fact that kills it, or the cheapest test it still has to pass.
after: Before you spend money or weeks, find the one fact that kills your idea. If it survives, you get the cheapest test it still has to pass.

before: Describe a purchase. Get payback, return and risk worked out, so you can decide whether to invest.
after: Work out whether a business purchase pays off: payback time, return and risk, with a clear recommendation and the assumptions behind it. It is for business spending, not personal stocks.

before: Give it a role and candidate profile. Get the best places to look, target companies and a week-by-week plan.
after: A plan for where to find the right people and how to spend your time looking. Give a role and a candidate profile, and you get ranked places to search, target companies and communities, and a week-by-week schedule.

before: Name the Euro NCAP test. Get its scenario and variants made, plotted and exported with scores.
after: Name the Euro NCAP test you care about and get its driving scenario built, varied, plotted and scored. The skill creates the starting scenario for the test, makes variants from it, and moves the scenarios between two simulators.

before: Describe your work for car makers. Get the right TISAX level, labels and gaps before the assessment.
after: If you sell to car makers, you learn which TISAX level you need, which labels to ask for, and which gaps to close before the assessment.

before: Give it carbon-13 tracing data. Get estimated metabolic fluxes, fit checks and a profile you can trust.
after: Give it carbon-13 tracing data. Get estimated metabolic fluxes, fit checks and a profile you can trust. Bring a carbon network with atom assignments. Use the result to plan your next step.

before: Describe how you take card payments. Get your PCI level, the right self-check form and gaps to fix.
after: Your card payment setup is checked against the PCI standard so you know your level, the right self-assessment form, and the gaps to fix. Describe how you take cards, such as online checkout, in person or by phone, and you get a clear route.

before: Name a job family. Get career levels, growth plans and a manager guide for career talks.
after: Name a job family and get clear career levels, growth plans and a guide for managers on career talks. People can see what each level expects and what to do to reach the next one.

before: Add four habits to your AI coder. Get smaller, simpler changes that state their assumptions and prove they work.
after: Your AI coder makes smaller, simpler changes and shows its thinking before it writes. Add four habits, and the code you get back states its assumptions, does only what you asked, touches only what it must, and proves it works.

before: Name a file too rotten to patch. Get a justified delete and rebuild that keeps the behaviour that worked.
after: When a file is too broken to patch, you get a deletion that is justified and a rebuild that keeps every behaviour that worked. Name the file, and the AI must make its case before it removes a single line.

before: Run it on your shipments. Get delivery times and costs side by side by carrier, to guide your carrier mix.
after: Your carriers are compared head to head, so you can pick the best default for each route or weight. Run it on your Shopify shipments and you see average transit days, on-time rate and shipping cost per order side by side.

before: Give it your cash, debts and currency exposure. Get a liquidity plan and ways to cut rate and exchange risk.
after: You get a plan to keep enough cash on hand, make idle money earn something, and limit damage from rate and currency swings. Share your balances, debts and foreign currency exposure, and the skill acts like a company treasurer.

before: Give it your invoices, bills and fixed costs. Get a 30, 60 and 90 day cash forecast with risks named.
after: A 30, 60 and 90 day cash forecast that answers the question: will I make payroll next month? You get a short chat summary and an Excel workbook, with named risks next to the numbers.

before: Give it your receivables, payables and stock. Get days outstanding, the cash cycle and where cash is stuck.
after: You find out how much cash is locked in customers who owe you, stock on shelves and bills you pay early, and where to free it.

before: Describe an infringement or paste a letter you got. Get a draft demand or options. Have a lawyer review.
after: Either a draft demand letter for someone copying your work, or a plain options memo for a letter you received. Describe the infringement or paste the letter, and you get a first version a lawyer can review and finish.

before: Give it single-cell counts with spliced reads. Get cell direction arrows, timing and the genes that drive them.
after: Single-cell data tells you which way cells seem to be heading, how far along they are, and which genes push them. Give it counts with spliced and unspliced reads, and you get arrows on the cell map, a timeline for each cell, and ranked driver genes.

before: Describe a re-org, tool change or layoff. Get the announcement, FAQ, manager talking points and a send plan.
after: The full message package for a re-org, tool change or layoff: the announcement, an FAQ, talking points for managers and a calendar of follow-ups. It is written for staff, not customers, and settles when to speak, in what order and what to leave unsaid.

before: Describe a code change. Get what it could break outside its own diff, and one proof it is safe.
after: Before you ship a change, you learn what it could break outside its own diff, and you get one piece of proof that it is safe.

before: Describe a system or process change. Get a change request with impact, risks, rollback steps and who to tell.
after: A formal change request for a system or process change, with impact, risks, rollback steps and who to tell. Describe the change and you get a document ready for approval.

before: Describe a re-org or tool switch. Get a rollout plan, message templates and a plan for pushback.
after: A re-org or tool switch gets a rollout plan, message templates and a plan for pushback, so people actually adopt it. Most changes fail in the rollout, not the design, and this plan is built around the stages people go through.

before: Give it a Python change. Get tests that fail whenever that change is broken, proven by code mutations.
after: Tests that fail whenever your Python change is broken, proven by deliberately breaking the code. Give it a change and the skill checks it is actually tested, not just passing.

before: Give it a commit range or pull request. Get a clean changelog entry grouped into added, changed and fixed.
after: A clean changelog entry you can paste into your file, grouped into added, changed and fixed. Give it a commit range or a pull request and it turns the raw history into what users and maintainers need to know.

before: Point it at a repo. Get a clear changelog built from the git history.
after: A readable changelog built straight from your git history, so you can see what changed this week without reading every commit. Point it at a repo and it groups changes by day for the last week, then by week.

before: Give it direct and partner sales costs. Get cost to serve, ROI by channel and the best mix.
after: Which sales channel really makes money? You get a clear verdict for each one: double down, maintain, defund or exit. Plus a suggested mix of direct and partner sales that holds up when costs shift.

before: Name a trait like curiosity. Get a plan to gather evidence from several people. Not medical advice.
after: A plan for judging a personal quality, like curiosity or persistence, without turning it into a grade that hurts the learner. You name the trait and the age band, and you get a way to collect evidence from several angles.

before: Find customers with disputed orders. Get their records tagged so you review their next orders. Changes live customer tags.
after: Customers who have lost you a dispute get a tag on their record, so you can review or hold their next orders. This one writes to your live Shopify store, so it starts in preview mode and shows you who would be tagged before anything changes.

before: Tell it the dispute reason. Get what proof to collect, where to find it in Shopify, and whether to accept instead.
after: Before you spend hours digging up files, you get a short checklist of exactly what proof your dispute needs. Tell it the reason on the dispute, and it sorts each item into have, get, check or not available, with the spot in Shopify where you can find it.

before: Give it your charts or app. Get colour palettes, colormaps and dark mode applied the right way.
after: MATLAB charts and apps that use one clean set of colours, with dark mode that works. You give it your figures or app, and it sets palettes, colormaps and themes the way MATLAB expects, instead of scattering colour values through your code.

before: Give it your data. Get clear charts and dashboards made with matplotlib, seaborn or plotly.
after: Hand over a dataset and a question, and get back a clean chart or a small dashboard you can drop into a report. The right chart type is chosen for you, so a trend becomes a line, a comparison becomes bars and a spread becomes a box plot.

before: Give it a Telegram group export. Get a ranked list of unmet needs, each backed by real quotes.
after: Thousands of group messages turn into a ranked list of problems people keep complaining about, with real quotes as proof. It reads a Telegram Desktop export and shows which needs are worth building something for.

before: Describe your chatbot job. Get conversation flows with questions, error recovery and graceful fallbacks.
after: A full conversation plan for your chatbot, so users reach their goal instead of hitting dead ends. You describe the bot's job, and you get its personality, the things it handles, the questions it asks and what it says when it gets confused.

before: Describe the tool you want inside ChatGPT. Get a working Apps SDK project with its server and screen.
after: A working starter project for a tool that runs inside ChatGPT, with its server and its on-screen panel. You describe what the app should do, and you get code that follows the current Apps SDK instead of guesses from old examples.

before: Give it your cart and checkout. Get a ranked list of fixes for guest checkout, fields, wallets and surprise costs.
after: A ranked fix list for your cart and checkout, so shoppers who already want the item can pay without a fight. You share your flow, and each problem comes with the change to make and the study behind it.

before: Describe what young children keep asking about. Get a project plan that follows their interests into deeper inquiry.
after: When young children keep asking about the same thing, like worms, shadows or bridges, you get a project plan that grows from their questions. Instead of a fixed unit, it starts from what you saw and heard and moves toward deeper inquiry.

before: Describe your time block. Get a plan for a long stretch of independent, choice-based work.
after: A plan for a long, uninterrupted stretch where students pick their own work and stay focused. You tell it how much time you really have and what is on offer, and you get a block that works in a real timetable.

before: Give it your text. Get a searchable store that finds passages by meaning, ready for question-answering.
after: A small searchable store for your documents that finds passages by meaning instead of exact words. Ask a question and it brings back the closest text, ready to feed into a question-answering app.

before: Describe your product and why people leave. Get a cancel flow, save offers and a failed-payment recovery plan.
after: A plan to keep more subscribers: a cancel flow that asks why, save offers that match each reason, and a way to win back failed payments.

before: Give it usage, engagement and support data. Get at-risk accounts scored with ideas for how to step in.
after: A scored list of customer accounts most likely to leave, each with a suggested next step. You share usage, engagement and support data, and every account gets a score from 0 (healthy) to 100 (about to go).

before: Describe your project. Get a CI/CD pipeline that builds, tests and ships across environments.
after: A build, test and release pipeline for your project, so code goes from push to live without manual steps. You describe your language, host and target, and you get ready-to-use config files.

before: Point it at a failing pull request. Get the cause of the failed GitHub check and a fix plan.
after: A red check on your pull request turns into a clear cause and a short plan to fix it. Point it at the PR, and it reads the logs from the failed GitHub Actions run, pulls out the lines that matter and tells you what went wrong.

before: Give it a big problem. Get what students control, can influence or only care about, so they act where it counts.
after: A big problem can leave students feeling either helpless or guilty. This sorts it into three rings: what they control, what they can influence, and what they can only care about.

before: Give it DOIs, paper titles or a messy bibliography. Get clean, checked BibTeX entries with duplicates removed.
after: A clean bibliography with every entry checked against the real paper. Give it DOIs, PubMed or arXiv IDs, paper titles or a messy BibTeX file, and get back tidy entries with duplicates removed.

before: Ask a question. Get a cited report with each claim checked against its source quote. Uses many tokens. Scrapes sites.
after: Ask a question and get a written report where each important claim is tied to a source and a quote you can check. It leaves a full run folder behind, so you can see how the answer was reached.

before: Give it a text. Get each claim checked against trusted sources and scored by confidence.
after: Paste a text and get a verdict on each claim in it, with a confidence score and the sources behind it. Instead of one true or false for the whole piece, you see exactly which sentence holds up and which does not.

before: Give it a hard question. Get a clear guess, a fair attempt to break it, the evidence and a tested answer.
after: Give it a hard question. Get a clear guess, a fair attempt to break it, the evidence and a tested answer. Bring the question or problem. Use the result to plan your next step.

before: Give it claims history. Get loss reserves, IBNR estimates and loss and combined ratios.
after: How much should an insurer set aside for claims that have happened but are not yet fully paid? You give it claims history, and you get reserve estimates, the incurred but not reported amount (IBNR) and the loss and combined ratios.

before: Give it your topic and group. Get the discussion format that fits, with steps to run it.
after: The right kind of class discussion for your goal, with steps to run it. A debate, a Socratic seminar and a think-pair-share all do different jobs.

before: Give it a OneRoster CSV set. Get broken links, bad encodings and manifest errors found, with fixes.
after: Find out why a student roster upload gets rejected before you send it. Give it your OneRoster CSV files, and it lists broken links between files, bad text encodings and manifest errors, each with a fix.

before: Give it a question about your teaching. Get a plan to collect evidence and act on what you find.
after: A plan for finding out whether a change in your teaching actually works. You write a question about your own practice, and you get a full cycle: how to gather evidence, how to read it, and what to do next.

before: Describe a class dynamic like cliques or new students. Get actions that help everyone feel part of the group.
after: Practical steps to make every student feel part of your class, aimed at the exact problem you face. Describe the group, such as cliques, an isolated child or new arrivals, and you get actions you can start this week.

before: Describe your room. Get a layout and materials plan that helps learners work on their own with calm moves between tasks.
after: A room plan that lets students find materials, work on their own and move between tasks calmly. You describe your room and what goes wrong, and you get a change list in order of cost and effort.

before: Describe your room and what feels off. Get layout, light and plant ideas for a calmer room. Not medical advice.
after: Ideas to make your room calmer using light, plants, natural materials and views, scaled to your budget. You describe the room and what feels off, and you get a plan you can do in stages.

before: Give it a tool or AI app and a subject. Get a check of how well it fits your teaching, with changes.
after: Before you bring an app or AI tool into a lesson, check whether it fits what you teach and how. You name the tool, the topic and your students, and you get a plain verdict with changes to make it work.

before: Say what to build with Claude. Get working code that calls the Claude API the right way.
after: Tell it what you want to build with Claude, and get working code that talks to the Claude API correctly. It uses the official software kit for your language, so function names and imports are real and not guessed.

before: Point it at Claude Code memory. Get what it learned reviewed, kept rules moved up and stale notes cut.
after: Claude Code keeps notes about your project as it works. This reviews those notes so the good ones become firm rules, and the stale ones get cut.

before: Tell it your work. Get lessons and exercises that make you faster with Claude, one step at a time.
after: Short lessons and exercises that make you faster with Claude, one step at a time and tuned to your own work. It asks one question about how you use Claude, then teaches the tricks that matter for you.

before: Give it an asset and its cleanup cost. Get the liability, yearly interest cost and journal entries worked out.
after: If you must clean up or remove an asset later, the cost counts today. You give the asset and the estimated cleanup cost, and you get the liability, the yearly interest cost and the journal entries for each year.

before: Give it your slow stock and past sales. Get when and how much to cut prices to sell out.
after: Give it your slow stock and past sales. Get when and how much to cut prices to sell out. Bring stock list with quantities and age. Use the result to plan your next step.

before: Give it study data that is safe to share. Get evidence profiles, cohort and survival summaries and privacy notes.
after: Give it study data that is safe to share. Get evidence profiles, cohort and survival summaries and privacy notes. Bring aggregate study data with small cells hidden. Use the result to plan your next step.

before: Give it de-identified case or trial data. Get a structured report draft and checks for gaps.
after: Give it de-identified case or trial data. Get a structured report draft and checks for gaps. Bring de-identified or synthetic facts. Use the result to plan your next step.

before: Point it at your AWS account. Get idle and unused resources listed, with the savings for each fix.
after: A list of AWS resources you pay for but do not use, with the savings from fixing each. Point it at your account and it reviews your spending, finds the waste and tells you what to switch off or shrink.

before: Give it your Python code. Get it running on rented GPUs, or live as a web API, with no server to manage.
after: Your Python code runs on rented GPUs, or goes live as a web endpoint, and you do not manage a server. You pay by the second, and everything shuts down to zero when idle.

before: Point it at your cloud setup files. Get open buckets, loose access rules and gaps ranked with fixes.
after: A ranked list of cloud settings that put you at risk, each with a fix. Point it at your infrastructure files or exported configs, and it finds open storage buckets, loose permissions and overly wide network rules.

before: Name your app and cloud. Get metrics, logs, traces and alerts set up to see health in real time.
after: Know when your app is slow or broken before your users tell you. You end up with a monitoring plan and the config to run it: metrics, logs, traces, dashboards and alert rules for your cloud.

before: Describe the cloud setup you need. Get Terraform, Pulumi or CloudFormation code that builds it the same way every time.
after: Describe the servers, networks and databases you want, and get code that builds them the same way every time. Nobody has to click through a console and hope they remember each step.

before: Point it at your project. Get it live on Cloudflare, with the link to open.
after: Point it at your project. Get it live on Cloudflare, with the link to open. Bring your project folder. Use the result to plan your next step.

before: Tell it what you need made or packed. Get a way to pick a co-packer and a plan to manage the deal.
after: A clear way to choose a contract manufacturer, and a plan to run the deal once you sign. It helps you avoid picking on price alone and finding out about quality problems after launch.

before: Point it at a set of changes. Get a review against your coding standards and your spec, side by side.
after: Two reviews of the same set of changes, side by side: does the code follow your team's standards, and does it do what the ticket asked?

before: Point it at messy code. Get the problem spots named and cleaned up with proven patterns.
after: Messy code gets a short list of named problems and a safe order for fixing them. The code ends up easier to read and change, and it still does the same thing.

before: Give it a code file. Get clear, professional comments and tidy-ups, with the logic left untouched.
after: Comments that read like one careful person wrote them, and code that still behaves exactly the same. It is meant for the last pass before a review, a handoff or going public.

before: Give it a tricky function. It writes the rules and edge cases first, then code that keeps them.
after: A tricky function gets its rules written down before any code, so off-by-one and empty-input bugs get caught early. Tests alone often miss these, because the bug lives in the contract, not the loop body.

before: Point it at code you need to understand. Get a line-by-line map of how it works before you hunt bugs.
after: Before you hunt for bugs, you get a slow, line-by-line understanding of what the code does. That cuts guessing, mixed-up facts and lost context in the later audit.

before: Point it at your code. Get docstrings, a README and usage guides that match what the code does.
after: Point it at your code. Get docstrings, a README and usage guides that match what the code does. Bring your code or project folder. Use the result to plan your next step.

before: Give it code. Get duplication, tight coupling and weak contracts flagged, with fixes. Uses Pragmatic Programmer principles.
after: Your code gets a score out of ten against the habits from The Pragmatic Programmer, plus a list of what to fix. It shows where repeated logic, tangled parts and unclear promises will make future changes expensive.

before: Give it your docs and code. Get each place the code breaks its own rules, with a fix.
after: Find the places where your code does something different from what your own docs say it should. These are the bugs a normal scanner misses, like a permission that is written down but never enforced.

before: Point it at a git repo. Get who owns the sensitive code and where one person is the only owner.
after: A map of who really owns your sensitive code, and where a single person is the only one who knows it. It turns git history into risk you can act on.

before: Give it messy code. Get named refactoring moves to apply in small safe steps, without changing what it does.
after: Messy code turns into a list of named moves you can apply one at a time, with tests passing after each. Nothing about what the code does should change.

before: Give it a markdown code review. Get one HTML page with severity tags and diffs that are easy to read.
after: A markdown code review becomes one HTML page that is easy to scan. You get a jump menu, diffs on one side, comments on the other, severity tags such as blocker and major, and the reviewer named at the bottom.

before: Describe a bug pattern. Get a tested Semgrep rule that finds it across your code.
after: Describe a bug pattern once and get a Semgrep rule that finds it everywhere in your code. The rule is tested, so it catches the bad cases and leaves safe code alone.

before: Point it at your Python, JavaScript, TypeScript or Go code. Get a ranked list of security gaps, each with a fix.
after: A ranked list of security gaps in your Python, JavaScript, TypeScript or Go code, each with a fix. You can also use it to write new code that is safe from the start.

before: Point it at your source code. Get security flaws found with static tools and rules you can add to CI.
after: Point it at your source code. Get security flaws found with static tools and rules you can add to CI. Bring your source code repository. Use the result to plan your next step.

before: Point it at code that works but is hard to read. Get a simpler version that behaves the same.
after: Code that works but is hard to read becomes simpler and behaves exactly the same. The test is whether a new teammate would understand the new version faster.

before: Before it writes loops or queries, it states the best approach and cost. Get code that avoids slow patterns.
after: Code that avoids slow patterns from the start. Before it writes a loop or a query, it states the best approach and what it will cost, so O(n squared) work and N+1 queries do not reach production.

before: Point it at a codebase. Get a product requirements document built from its screens, data and flows.
after: A product requirements document built from the code you already have. It is written in plain business language, yet detailed enough for an engineer or an AI agent to rebuild each page and endpoint.

before: Give it MATLAB code. Get tracing added so you can see where time goes and where errors start.
after: Your MATLAB code gains tracing, so you can see where time goes and where errors start. Each function reports what it did, how long it took and whether it failed.

before: Point it at code you own. Get proven, exploitable bugs with steps to reproduce and fixes.
after: Point it at code you own. Get proven, exploitable bugs with steps to reproduce and fixes. Bring the code or system you own. Use the result to plan your next step.

before: Point it at your code. Get an HTML report of design improvements, then work through the one you pick.
after: An HTML report of design improvements for your codebase, then a guided session on the one you pick. The focus is turning shallow, tangled modules into deep ones that are easier to test and easier for an AI to navigate.

before: Point it at a codebase. Get two guides that take a new engineer from first day to deep knowledge.
after: Two guides that take a new engineer from day one to deep knowledge of your codebase. One is for senior people who need the reasons behind choices; the other is for those who need to get started now.

before: Name your audience. Get a step-by-step tour file that links real files and lines for a new teammate.
after: A guided walkthrough of your code, saved as a tour file that opens inside VS Code and jumps to real files and lines. Each tour is written for one person, so it tells them what matters and what to do next.

before: Describe the change you want. Get a handoff note with scope, checks and stop rules for a coding agent.
after: A handoff note that lets a coding agent run on its own and come back with work a person can review. It is made for overnight or background jobs where you will not be watching.

before: Finish a coding session. Get what slowed your AI down and the changes that would help next time.
after: After a coding session, you learn what slowed your AI down and what changes to your setup would help next time. The fixes target the working environment, not your prompts.

before: Describe a coding task. Get a short plan with scope, ordered action items, tests and open questions.
after: A short plan you can act on, produced before anyone touches the code. It lists what is in scope, what is not, and an ordered checklist from discovery to rollout.

before: Paste a cold email and what you know of the prospect. Get claims tested, legal basics checked, and a tighter version.
after: A careful second opinion on a cold email before you hit send. It tests every claim about the prospect against their real page, checks legal basics, and returns a tighter version.

before: Name your buyer and offer. Get cold emails, follow-ups and a sending setup that gets replies.
after: Cold emails that read like a sharp person wrote them, plus follow-ups and a sending setup that keeps you out of spam. The goal is replies that turn into meetings.

before: Pick a collection. Get in-stock products moved to the top and sold-out ones to the bottom. Changes your live store.
after: Products in stock move to the top of a Shopify collection and sold-out ones drop to the bottom. It changes your live store, so shoppers see what they can actually buy first.

before: Give it your colour tokens. Get light and dark theme pairs checked for readability, with the closest passing colours.
after: Your colour tokens get checked for readability in both light and dark themes, and each failure comes with the closest colour that passes. Fix a token once and it is fixed everywhere it is used.

before: Give it your source and target tables. Get a column-by-column map with rules, gaps and decisions to review.
after: A column-by-column map from your source tables to your target tables, with the rules for each, the gaps, and decisions someone must still make. It saves your team from guessing where each field comes from.

before: Give it an API doc or script. Get a command-line tool that returns clean JSON and handles sign-in.
after: A real command-line tool you can run by name from any folder. Give it an API doc, a script or a few curl examples, and get a tool that returns clean JSON and handles sign-in.

before: Give it social posts. Get what people ask, complain about and want, in their own words. Collects data from websites.
after: What people ask, complain about and want, in their own words, pulled from social comments. Use it for product research, content ideas, copy and objection handling.

before: Say the word. Get your changes committed, pushed and opened as a GitHub pull request in one go.
after: Say the word. Get your changes committed, pushed and opened as a GitHub pull request in one go. Bring your changes in a git repo. Use the result to plan your next step.

before: Give it a commit message. Get a plain version that sounds like a careful engineer, with no AI filler.
after: A commit message that reads like a careful engineer wrote it at the end of a real day, with no AI filler. It keeps the Conventional Commits format.

before: Stage your changes. Get a short commit message that says what changed and why.
