before: Give it your leads. Get them scored on fit and activity and sorted into ranked tiers.
after: Your leads in a ranked list, with hot ones at the top so your team calls them first. Give your ideal customer profile, the activity signals you track and a list of leads.

before: Give it your CRM leads and ad history. Learn if your lead source fields are good enough to link leads to ads.
after: A yes or no on whether your CRM's source fields are good enough to link leads to the ads that brought them. Give it CRM rows and ad history rows, plus a binding that says which CRM fields join to which ad account, platform and entity type.

before: Give it your CRM lead export. Get each lead linked to the paid channel and ad that brought it in.
after: A table with one row per lead showing which paid channel and ad brought it in. Give it a CRM lead export. The skill reads click IDs and UTM tags in a set order: current click, current UTM, first-touch click, then first-touch UTM.

before: Say who you are training. Get a program, a 360 review form, a coaching guide and a succession plan.
after: Say who you are training. Get a program, a 360 review form, a coaching guide and a succession plan. Bring who you are training and their level. Use the result to plan your next step.

before: Give it your landing page, signup or checkout. Get the leaks ranked, plus tests to run in order.
after: A ranked list of where your page, signup or checkout loses people, and a series of tests to fix them in the right order. It works in seven phases and asks before every decision.

before: Describe your idea. Get a one-page lean canvas with problem, solution, channels, costs and revenue.
after: Your business idea on a single page, with every box filled in and the riskiest guesses visible. Describe the product, the customer and what you know about the market.

before: Describe your product plan. Get a smaller scope, a six-week bet and features to say no to. Uses Shape Up.
after: A smaller plan that you can actually finish: a fixed six-week bet, a clear scope, and a list of features you chose not to build.

before: Describe a class activity. Get a way to record children's learning, share it with families and plan next steps.
after: Describe a class activity. Get a way to record children's learning, share it with families and plan next steps. Bring the activity or investigation. Use the result to plan your next step.

before: Give it a learning goal. Get specific ways to engage learners, present content and let them show what they know.
after: A set of specific choices for how learners take part, take in content and show what they know, all for one learning goal. Give the goal and how you plan to teach it now.

before: Give it a lease contract. Get the lease liability, right-of-use asset and yearly entries under IFRS 16 or ASC 842.
after: The numbers for a lease on your books: the liability, the right-of-use asset and the entries for each year. Give the contract terms. The skill first checks whether it is a lease at all, then settles the lease term, which payments count and which discount rate applies.

before: Give it ledger and subledger data. Get matches, breaks and a likely cause for each break.
after: A reconciliation that shows what matches between your general ledger and subledger, what does not, and a likely reason for each gap. Supply both extracts for the same entity and date.

before: Pick a daily scan, a topic or an incident. Get a short briefing from your email, calendar and files. Not legal advice.
after: Pick a daily scan, a topic or an incident. Get a short briefing from your email, calendar and files. Not legal advice. Bring the question or situation (for topic or incident). Use the result to plan your next step.

before: Tell it about a dispute. Get a notice telling staff which records to keep. A first draft, not legal advice.
after: A notice telling staff which records they must keep when a dispute is likely, written as a first draft for a lawyer to review. Tell it about the matter.

before: Name the request, such as a data access request. Get a draft reply and a flag when a lawyer must review.
after: Name the request, such as a data access request. Get a draft reply and a flag when a lawyer must review. Bring the type of request. Use the result to plan your next step.

before: Name a negotiation or review meeting. Get background, key issues, questions to ask, then action items. Not legal advice.
after: A one-page prep sheet for a legal meeting, so you walk in knowing the background, the issues and what to ask. Name the meeting. The skill works out its type, such as a deal review, board session, vendor call or dispute, then decides what prep that type needs.

before: Describe a deal or issue. Get each risk rated by how bad and how likely. Not legal advice.
after: A rating for each legal risk in a deal or issue, scored on two scales so you can tell which ones need attention now. Describe the situation.

before: Paste a lesson and describe your class. Get likely barriers and which ones design can fix. It does not diagnose anyone.
after: A list of places your lesson is likely to trip learners up, before you teach it. Paste the task and describe your class, such as English learners, attention needs or wide reading levels.

before: Give it what you want to learn from a visit. Get look-fors and a way to record evidence.
after: A focused observation form for classroom visits, with the specific things to look for and a way to record what you see as evidence. Say what you want to learn from the visit and why it is happening: coaching, peer learning, quality checks or research.

before: Give it today's topic and last lesson. Get a starter that brings back what students know and links to the new content.
after: A short lesson opening that brings back what students already know and links it to today's topic. Give today's topic, what you taught last time and the level of your class.

before: Give it a teaching question. Get a full lesson study plan, from shared planning to the research lesson.
after: A four-meeting plan for a teaching team to study one problem in their own classrooms, from first question to shared findings. You skip the guesswork about what each meeting should produce.

before: Give it your lesson stages. Get a check for each stage, so you know who has it before moving on.
after: Know who has understood before you move on, not after the test. Give it your lesson stages and you get a planned check for each one, so quiet students cannot hide behind the confident few.

before: Point it at a Python project. Get which library changes came after the AI's training and where your code uses them.
after: AI models write code from what they learned before a cutoff date. If your project pins newer library versions, the model may use old methods.

before: Describe the document. Get an ODT file, or a conversion to Word, PDF or HTML.
after: Make a text document from a plain description, then turn it into the format the other person needs. You get an ODT file, or a copy in Word, PDF or HTML, without opening a word processor.

before: Describe the slides. Get an ODP deck, or a conversion to PowerPoint or PDF.
after: Describe a presentation and get a finished deck file, then turn it into PowerPoint or PDF for whoever needs it. No slide editor needed on your side.

before: Describe the sheet. Get an ODS file with formulas and charts, or a conversion to Excel or CSV.
after: A working spreadsheet with formulas and charts, built from a plain description, and ready to open in Excel or save as CSV. You describe the sheet and skip the manual setup.

before: Describe a company for sale. Get a ranked list of likely buyers, strategic and financial, with fit notes.
after: Before you sell a company, you need to know who might buy it. This builds a ranked list of likely buyers, with a reason each one fits and a sensible order to call them.

before: Tell it the work. Get Linear issues read, created or updated for you.
after: Tell your AI what work needs tracking and it reads, creates or updates the Linear issues for you. No tab switching, no copying details by hand.

before: Describe your site. Get a plan for link building, digital PR, brand mentions and local listings, with linkable ideas.
after: A plan to earn links and mentions that point at your site, with ideas people will want to link to. You stop sending bulk pitches that get ignored.

before: Share a link that looks wrong. Get the tags and image fixes so it shows a rich card everywhere.
after: When you share a link and it shows a bare URL or the wrong picture, this finds why and gives you the fix. Your pages then show a proper card on Facebook, LinkedIn, X, WhatsApp, Telegram, Slack and Discord.

before: Give it your past accounts and drivers. Get income, balance sheet and cash flow models that tie together.
after: Income statement, balance sheet and cash flow built so they tie out, with the balance check proving it. Give it your past accounts and your key drivers and you get a model you can stress and trust.

before: Give it your LinkedIn Ads exports. Get a checked audit of your Insight Tag, audiences, lead forms, creative, bids and budgets.
after: A checked audit of your LinkedIn Ads account that separates what the data shows from what to try. Give it your exports and you get findings tied to the numbers they came from.

before: Paste a post. Get a comment that adds something new instead of agreeing, in your voice.
after: Paste a post. Get a comment that adds something new instead of agreeing, in your voice. Bring the post text. Use the result to plan your next step.

before: Say your goal. Get content pillars, positioning and a posting rhythm you can keep.
after: A LinkedIn plan you can keep: who you write for, what you stand for, what you will not post about, and how often you will show up.

before: Give a topic and angle. Get a LinkedIn post built on a tested opening line for your goal.
after: A LinkedIn post that opens with a line chosen for what you want it to do: draw comments, reposts, likes or saves. You pick the goal first and the opening follows.

before: Say who you want to reach. Get a commenting list, connection notes and a plan, all sent by you.
after: A plan to grow your reach on LinkedIn by commenting first and reaching out second, and every message is sent by you. Tell it who you want to reach and it builds the list and the notes.

before: Give it a story or idea. Get a LinkedIn post, carousel script or poll that you post yourself.
after: A LinkedIn post, carousel script or poll you can post yourself, built from your own story or idea. It also checks drafts you already wrote.

before: Describe your profile. Get a stronger headline, About section and experience bullets.
after: A LinkedIn profile that tells people why to contact you. You describe yours and get a sharper headline, About section and experience bullets, fixed in the order that pays off most.

before: Paste your own LinkedIn numbers. Get which posts worked, why reach changed and a test to run next.
after: A plain reading of your own LinkedIn numbers: which posts worked, why reach changed, and one test to run next. It is careful not to claim more than the data supports.

before: Run it after a change. It runs your project's checks, fixes real failures and reports what did not run.
after: A clear pass or fail on your project's lint and type checks after a change, with an honest line for any check that never ran.

before: Paste your theme code or say what you need. Get correct Liquid for products, carts and loops.
after: Working Shopify Liquid code for your theme, without trial and error. Paste your theme code or say what you need, and get the right objects, filters and loops for products, collections and carts.

before: Get every product scored on missing descriptions, images, SEO, weight, barcode and cost, worst first.
after: Every product in your store scored on how complete its data is, worst first, so you know exactly what to fix. It only reads, and changes nothing in your shop.

before: Give it a topic. Get the key academic papers found from open databases and sorted by theme.
after: A starting set of real academic papers on your topic, found from free databases and sorted by theme. You can trust each paper because it was found in this session.

before: Give it a topic. Get a structured review of sources chosen by clear rules, with findings synthesised.
after: A written literature review where every source was chosen by rules you can state, not by whatever came up first. Give it a topic and get findings drawn together by theme.

before: Pick a small open model and your data. Get it downloaded, trained on your examples and ready to chat with.
after: A small open model, downloaded, trained on your examples and ready to chat with, without writing training code from scratch. You pick the model and data and get working commands.

before: Give it a running web app or API you own. Get weaknesses found by safe probing.
after: A list of weaknesses found in a running web app or API that you own, found by safe probing from the outside. You get a report with how to fix each one.

before: Describe the effect. Get a frame-by-frame audio chain with filters, EQ and level meters.
after: A chain of audio processing that runs on sound as it plays, with filters, equaliser and level meters you can tweak while it runs. Describe the effect you want and get MATLAB code that does it.

before: Point it at a bug. Get the program run with breakpoints, so you see exact values and where it goes wrong.
after: Instead of guessing from error text, run the program and stop it where the bug lives. You see the exact values at that moment and trace back to the cause.

before: Paste what the buyer said. Get what it really means, a reply that has worked before and proof to use.
after: When a buyer says "too expensive" or "we're talking to a rival", you need an answer now. Paste what they said and get what they likely mean, a reply that has worked before and proof to back it.

before: Describe the screen bug. Get your web or Electron app opened, tried out and fixed step by step.
after: Describe the screen bug and your web or Electron app is opened, clicked through and fixed in a loop, until it works. You watch the problem disappear.

before: Describe the analysis or lesson. Get a MATLAB live script with text, equations and figures you can run.
after: A MATLAB live script, as plain text you can open and run, with explanations, equations and figures built in. Describe the analysis or lesson and get a runnable notebook.

before: Say your model and GPU. Get a fine-tuning plan and code with Unsloth, sized to your memory, ready to export.
after: Say your model and GPU. Get a fine-tuning plan and code with Unsloth, sized to your memory, ready to export. Bring base model. Use the result to plan your next step.

before: Give it your site. Get an llms.txt file that tells AI tools which pages and facts matter most.
after: An llms.txt file for your site, a plain list that tells AI tools which pages and facts matter most. You choose what they see first instead of letting them guess.

before: Give it a component or page. Get loading, success, error and empty states added, so users always know what is happening.
after: A screen that always tells people what is going on. Give it a component or page and it adds loading, empty, error and success states, so nobody stares at a blank box.

before: Say what hardware you have. Get Ollama and Open WebUI running local models, tuned for your graphics card.
after: Run AI models on your own computer, tuned for your graphics card, with a chat screen in your browser. Say what hardware you have and get Ollama and Open WebUI working together.

before: Give it a model. Get a smaller file that runs on your laptop or Mac with no GPU, plus the run steps.
after: A smaller version of an AI model that runs on your laptop, a Mac or a plain CPU with no GPU. Give it a model and get a compact GGUF file plus the steps to run it.

before: Name your model and computer. Get it running on a Mac, a plain CPU or a non-NVIDIA graphics card.
after: An AI model running on a Mac, a plain CPU or a non-Nvidia graphics card, with no CUDA needed. Name the model and your computer and get the commands that start it.

before: Name a place near your learners. Get lessons that tie your content to that place, its community and its heritage.
after: Lessons that start from a real place near your students and still cover your curriculum. Name the place and the content and get an inquiry plan where the place is the text.

before: Describe your service business and area. Get a local search audit, listing fixes and a plan for more reviews.
after: A local search plan for a business that serves customers at their location, like repair, heating, plumbing or cleaning. Describe your business and area and get an audit, fixes and a review plan.

before: Say what must work in production. Get logs, metrics and alerts added so problems show up fast.
after: Code that tells you what it is doing in production, so when something breaks you can see what happened. Say what must work and get logs, metrics and alerts added to match.

before: Describe your app's users. Get a login and permissions plan, or a review of the one you have.
after: Describe your app's users. Get a login and permissions plan, or a review of the one you have. Bring a description of your app and its users. Use the result to plan your next step.

before: Describe your brand. Get logo directions with colors, type, file formats and usage rules.
after: A logo brief and two or three distinct logo directions, each with colors, fonts, file formats and rules for using it. You can hand it to a designer or an image tool and know what to ask for.

before: Describe your brand. Get several logo directions, from wordmarks to symbols, each with the reasoning and how to use it.
after: Describe your brand. Get several logo directions, from wordmarks to symbols, each with the reasoning and how to use it. Bring your brand name and tone of voice. Use the result to plan your next step.

before: Describe how your AI gets worse in long chats. Get the likely cause and a fix to try.
after: A named cause for why your AI gets worse as a chat grows, and a fix you can try today. Long chats fail in a few known ways, and each one needs a different cure.

before: Give it a long AI session. Get a structured summary that keeps files, decisions and next steps.
after: Give it a long AI session. Get a structured summary that keeps files, decisions and next steps. Bring the long chat or its log. Use the result to plan your next step.

before: Say what you are writing, such as a case study or whitepaper. Get a clear outline and structure that avoids padding.
after: A clear outline for one long piece, such as a case study, whitepaper, research report or ebook, where every section earns its place. It aims to stop the two common failures: stretching a short idea with filler, and piling on facts with no spine.

before: Give it an article, newsletter or transcript. Get an X or LinkedIn post that works even if nobody clicks.
after: A post for X or LinkedIn that is worth reading even if nobody clicks your link. The usual summary plus link performs badly because all the value sits somewhere else.

before: Give it a goal that takes days. Get helpers and schedules set up to work on it.
after: A set-up that lets your AI work toward a goal that takes days, without losing what it learned along the way. It acts like a chief of staff: it plans, hands out work, and keeps notes.

before: Name your model. Get a method and code to make it read much longer documents than it was trained for.
after: A method, with working code, for making a language model read documents far longer than it was trained on. This is for people training or running models, and it needs Python and a GPU.

before: Name what to tune. Get a local page with sliders and pickers to adjust the look by eye.
after: A small local web page where you change the look of something with sliders and pickers, and see the result as you go. You choose by eye, not by typing numbers into a chat.

before: Describe your offer. Get honest wording that shows what people lose by waiting, without fear tactics.
after: Messaging that shows what people lose by putting off a decision, written with real facts and without scare tactics. Used well, loss framing creates honest urgency.

before: Point it at a Lovable export. Get the Lovable tags, branding and filler files removed so the project is yours.
after: A project export with every trace of Lovable removed, so the code reads as your own before you ship or open-source it. It covers fifteen places where the tool leaves marks.

before: Give it a big model and your GPU size. Get a fine-tune that trains under 1 percent of the model and fits.
after: A fine-tuning setup that trains less than one percent of a large model, so it fits on a single GPU. It uses small add-on layers called adapters, which can be around 6 MB instead of a 14 GB full copy.

before: Give it a task students resist. Get why it drains motivation and a redesign built on choice, success and connection.
after: A diagnosis of why a task drains students' motivation, plus a redesigned version that keeps the same rigor. It treats low motivation as a response to the task, not as a flaw in the student.

before: Paste 1 to 3 star app reviews. Get a ranked brief of risks, repeat problems and what to fix first.
after: A ranked brief from your 1 to 3 star app reviews that shows which ones are urgent, which repeat, and what to fix first. It stops you treating every angry review as equally important.

before: Get your top-spending customers tagged and exported, ready for a loyalty program. Adds tags to live customer records.
after: A list of your best customers, tagged inside Shopify and exported, ready to invite into a loyalty program or a VIP campaign. It changes live customer records, so run it in preview first.

before: Give it vibration or sensor signals from a motor or pump. Get features ready for fault detection.
after: Give it vibration or sensor signals from a motor or pump. Get features ready for fault detection. Bring evenly sampled sensor data. Use the result to plan your next step.

before: Give it your jobs and machines. Get a job order that finishes everything sooner.
after: A job order for your machines that finishes everything sooner, or meets due dates, while keeping each job's steps in the right sequence. This is the classic job shop problem.

before: Describe the inspection job. Get a system that finds defects, counts parts or measures them.
after: An inspection system that finds defects, counts parts or measures them from camera images, matched to your problem. It runs in MATLAB with the Visual Inspection Toolbox.

before: Describe your product. Get a style guide with a magazine feel: serif type, tidy grids and easy reading.
after: Describe your product. Get a style guide with a magazine feel: serif type, tidy grids and easy reading. Bring a description of your product. Use the result to plan your next step.

before: Give it a product photo and selling points. Get test versions that change one thing each, plus a review sheet.
after: A product image test you can learn from, not just a pile of extra pictures. Each version differs from the control in one thing only, and you write down which one you expect to win and why before you run it.

before: Give it a product photo and selling points. Get a main image with the copy laid on. Your image model draws it.
after: A square main image for your product with selling-point text laid on it, built to stay readable at thumbnail size. Your image model draws it; Claude writes the instructions.

before: Name the package to upgrade. Get a staged plan that checks what breaks and tests each step.
after: A staged plan to move one package to a new major version, with a clear picture of what will break and tests after every step.

before: Describe your team and role. Get meeting rhythms, one-on-ones and the tasks that most raise your team's output.
after: A tuned management routine for your team, built on Andy Grove's High Output Management. It judges every habit by one test: does it raise what your team produces?

before: Give it your management team. Get skill standards, a 360 feedback form and a plan to support managers who struggle.
after: A plan to measure how well your managers manage, and to help the ones who struggle. It links management quality to team health and people leaving.

before: Name your paper topic. Get a packet of current sources, competing findings and background, each with its link.
after: A research packet for your paper: current sources, studies that disagree, and background reading, each with its link. The default target is 60 checked, distinct references, organised as a claim-to-source map instead of a loose list.

before: Give it a paper or proposal. Get a fair, evidence-based review with claim checks, method critique and revision steps.
after: A fair, evidence-based draft review of a paper or proposal that a human reviewer can edit and sign. It covers claim checks, method critique and clear revision steps.

before: Give it a markdown outline. Get one HTML slide deck you present with arrow keys, with speaker notes.
after: One HTML file that is your slide deck: open it in any browser, move with the arrow keys, show speaker notes and print to PDF.

before: Give it a long markdown file. Get one HTML page with a contents bar, search and light interactivity.
after: One tidy HTML page built from a long markdown file, with a contents bar that follows you, a search box and copy buttons on code.

before: Name the data source and series. Get MATLAB code that pulls Bloomberg, FRED, Haver or Datastream data.
after: Name the data source and series. Get MATLAB code that pulls Bloomberg, FRED, Haver or Datastream data. Bring the provider. Use the result to plan your next step.

before: Name a market. Get a sourced report where every claim has a source, and sizing shows its assumptions.
after: A market report where every claim points to a source you can check, and market size shows its working. You can defend it in front of a board or an investor.

before: Give it your market. Get market size two ways, survey sample sizes and segments scored.
after: Your market size worked out two ways, a survey sample that holds up for each segment you report, and a score for which segments are real markets.

before: Give it a market or product idea. Get a TAM, SAM and SOM estimate built top-down and bottom-up, with sources.
after: A market size estimate for your idea, shown as TAM, SAM and SOM and built three ways so you can see if the numbers agree.

before: Give it past spend and results by channel. Get low and high forecasts for a new budget, with diminishing returns built in.
after: Low and high forecasts for a new marketing budget, based on your past spend and results, with diminishing returns built in. The model does not assume that doubling spend doubles results.

before: Paste your ad or page copy. Get each claim sorted as fine, needs proof or cut, with safer wording. Not legal advice.
after: Every claim in your ad or page copy sorted into fine, needs proof or cut, with safer wording that keeps the energy. This is a check for risk, not legal advice, and a lawyer should confirm anything high-stakes.

before: Run it on your customers. Get who agreed to email and SMS marketing, and who did not, for compliance.
after: A count of how many of your Shopify customers agreed to email and SMS marketing, and how many did not. It is useful for privacy reviews and for knowing your real reachable audience.

before: Give it your MATLAB files. Get them uploaded to GitHub or MATLAB Drive, plus an Open in MATLAB Online link.
after: Your MATLAB files online, with a link that opens them in MATLAB Online in one click. Anyone you send it to can run your code without installing anything.

before: Say which database and table. Get working code to read, filter, write and update rows from MATLAB.
after: Working MATLAB code that reads from and writes to your database, with safe habits built in. Tell it the database and table, and it writes the connection, the queries and the updates.

before: Ask how a MATLAB function works. Get the right syntax from the official docs, with fewer wrong guesses.
after: The right MATLAB syntax, taken from the official MathWorks pages, instead of a function call that is almost right. Ask how a function works and it finds the page that answers it.

before: Give it a MATLAB function. Get clear help text with a summary line, syntax lines and See Also links.
after: Help text for a MATLAB function that shows up properly when someone types help or doc. You hand over the function and get the comment block back in MathWorks style.

before: Name the MathWorks products. Get them installed from the command line, the same way each time.
after: Name the MathWorks products. Get them installed from the command line, the same way each time. Bring operating system. Use the result to plan your next step.

before: Give it code that runs out of memory. Get the cause found, fixed and measured, with a short report.
after: A MATLAB script that no longer runs out of memory, with proof of how much it saved. You give it the code that crashes or crawls, and it finds what is eating the memory, changes it and measures again.

before: Name the package. Get it installed, updated or removed, with dependency errors sorted.
after: Name the package. Get it installed, updated or removed, with dependency errors sorted. Bring the package name. Use the result to plan your next step.

before: Point it at a MATLAB install. Get a list of every product and add-on package in it.
after: A clean list of every product and add-on package inside one MATLAB install. Point it at the install folder, or just name the release, and see what you actually have.

before: Say how your project is laid out. Get a matlab.toml with paths, dependencies and scripts set up.
after: A matlab.toml file that sets up your project: its folders, search paths, dependencies and scripts that run on open or close. You describe how the project is laid out and get a file that fits.

before: Give it your results. Get a PDF, Word or HTML report built with titles, chapters, tables and charts.
after: A finished report in PDF, Word or HTML, built from MATLAB code, with a title page, chapters, tables and charts. Give it your results and get a document that updates whenever you rerun it.

before: Give it code with passwords or API keys. Get them moved into the MATLAB Vault, not left in the file.
after: Passwords, tokens and keys taken out of your MATLAB code and kept in the MATLAB Vault, so a shared file never leaks them. You give it a script with credentials in plain text and get the safe version back.

before: Give it MATLAB code to time. Get repeatable performance tests that measure run time with sound statistics.
after: Repeatable MATLAB speed tests that tell you how long code really takes, with enough runs to trust the number. Give it the code to time and get a test class ready to run.

before: Give it slow code. Get the real slowdown found, fixed and measured, with no made-up speed claims.
after: Slow MATLAB code made faster by fixing the real bottleneck, with measured proof and no invented speed claims. You hand over slow code and get the cause, the fix and the numbers.

before: Point it at your tests. Get them run and filtered, with failures, coverage gaps and CI set up.
after: Your MATLAB tests run, filtered and explained. You get a clear pass and fail count, the reason for each failure, which lines are not covered by tests, and a build file for continuous integration.

before: Give it MATLAB code. Get C, C++ or CUDA code that is checked and tuned for speed.
after: MATLAB code turned into C, C++ or CUDA that has been checked against the original, and tuned for speed. Give it a function and say what you need it to run on.

before: Say which Python library you need. Get MATLAB code that calls it, with setup and errors fixed.
after: MATLAB code that calls a Python library and works, with the setup problems fixed. Tell it which library you need, such as pandas or scikit-learn, and it writes the calls and gets the environment right.

before: Give it MATLAB code. Get class-based unit tests with fixtures, mocks and app tests that you can run.
after: A set of MATLAB unit tests you can run today, written as classes with edge cases covered. Give it your code and get tests that check what it does, not how it does it.

before: Point it at an MCP server. Get a ranked list of attack risks, each with a fix.
after: A ranked list of the ways someone could attack your MCP server, with a fix for each. Point it at the server and see where an attacker or a confused AI could do damage.

before: Give it your MCP config files. Get a list of server packages that can change under you, before you approve them.
after: A list of the tool servers in your MCP config that could change under you, found before you approve them. It reads your config files without running anything, so nothing can start by accident.

before: Point it at an MCP server you run. Get a checklist of fixes for transport, auth, access and logging.
after: A checklist of fixes that locks down an MCP server you run. It covers the connection, who may sign in, what each user may do and what gets logged.

before: Point it at your MCP server. Get it hosted, scaled and packaged so others can install it.
after: Your MCP server running online and ready for others to install. It covers hosting, scaling and packaging, so people can use it remotely or install it on their own computers.

before: Say how people will connect to your MCP server. Get correct OAuth sign-in built into it.

before: Give it a role and market pay data. Get a pay range and a clear method you can explain to leaders.
after: A pay range for a role, built from market data, with a method you can explain to leaders. It also shows whether current pay is competitive.

before: Give it a role or pay data. Get market ranges, outliers and equity grant models. Not pay or tax advice.
after: A market pay check for a role, a scan of your pay data for outliers and a model of stock grants. It helps you set offers and plan raises.

before: Give it your pay goals and team size. Get pay bands, bonus ideas and a total pay statement outline. Not legal advice.
after: An outline of your total pay offer: pay bands, bonus ideas, benefits and a statement showing employees the full value. It is a draft, not legal advice.

before: Run it on your payouts. Get each one matched to the orders that funded it, with gaps flagged.
after: Each Shopify Payments payout matched to the orders that funded it, with gaps flagged so you can trace a missing dollar. It reads data only and changes nothing.

before: Give it your timesheets. Get hours totalled by person, every oddity flagged, and a run ready for your line by line approval.
after: Give it your timesheets. Get hours totalled by person, every oddity flagged, and a run ready for your line by line approval. Bring pay period and pay date. Use the result to plan your next step.

before: Describe your plans. Get upgrade screens, trigger moments and copy that convert free users.
after: Describe your plans. Get upgrade screens, trigger moments and copy that convert free users. Bring your plans and what is free or paid. Use the result to plan your next step.

before: Give it several RF PCB parts. Get them cascaded with extra parts added and S-parameters exported.
after: Several RF circuit board parts joined end to end into one circuit, with extra components added and results saved as a standard Touchstone file. It runs in MATLAB.

before: Name the band and split. Get a power divider or coupler designed and its response plotted.
after: A power splitter or coupler designed for your band and split ratio, with its response plotted so you can see if it works. It runs in MATLAB.

before: Set a goal such as wider bandwidth or smaller area. Get PCB sizes tuned by search to meet it.
after: Set a goal such as wider bandwidth or smaller area. Get PCB sizes tuned by search to meet it. Bring starting PCB design in MATLAB. Use the result to plan your next step.

before: Give it a finished PCB design. Get Gerber files with connectors, ready to send to a maker.
after: Gerber files for a finished RF board, with the right connectors attached and formatted for the company that will make it. It runs in MATLAB.

before: Give it a Gerber, ODB++ or Allegro file. Get its nets, layers and stack listed and ready to use.
after: Give it a Gerber, ODB++ or Allegro file. Get its nets, layers and stack listed and ready to use. Bring a Gerber, ODB++ or Allegro file. Use the result to plan your next step.

before: Name your board material. Get a substrate, conductor and layer stack set up with loss included.
after: Pick your board material and walk away with a substrate, a metal and a layer stack that behave like the real thing, loss included. Every RF board design starts here, and wrong material numbers ruin every result after it.

before: Say which part you need, such as an inductor or balun. Get it designed and checked.
after: Say which part you need, such as an inductor or balun. Get it designed and checked. Bring the part type. Use the result to plan your next step.

before: Give it a PCB layout. Get voltage drop, current density and rule checks on its power nets.
after: Voltage drop and hot spots on your power rails, found before the board is built. Load a layout and see where copper is too thin, where a via carries too much current and which rails miss their voltage margin.

before: Give it pass band and rejection needs. Get a PCB filter designed and its response plotted.
after: Say what band you need to pass and what you need to block, and get a printed-circuit filter designed with its response plotted. You do not have to know which filter type fits.

before: Give it a PCB design. Get S-parameters, insertion loss and fields computed with the right solver.
after: Know how much signal your RF board part loses, reflects and radiates before you build it. You get S-parameters, insertion loss and field plots from a solver chosen to match the shape of your design.

before: Give it impedance and layer needs. Get microstrip, stripline or paired traces sized and checked.
after: Trace widths and spacings that hit your impedance target, sized and checked in one pass. Ask for microstrip, stripline, coplanar or a differential pair and get the geometry plus crosstalk figures.

before: Describe a via transition. Get a via modeled with pads and return vias and its signal quality checked.
after: A via is where signals on a board often go wrong. Describe the layer change and get a model of it, with pads, antipads and ground return vias set, and a check of its signal quality.

before: Give it a target sequence. Get primer pairs checked for temperature, off-target matches and clear coordinates.
after: Give it a target sequence. Get primer pairs checked for temperature, off-target matches and clear coordinates. Bring target sequence or coordinates. Use the result to plan your next step.

before: Give it a PDF and the format you want. Get a faithful Markdown, HTML, Word or JSON copy with tables kept intact.
after: Give it a PDF and the format you want. Get a faithful Markdown, HTML, Word or JSON copy with tables kept intact. Bring the PDF file. Use the result to plan your next step.

before: Give it a PDF or a brief. Get the text pulled out or a new PDF with its layout checked.
after: Read a PDF without trusting raw text alone, or make a new one and see for yourself that it looks right. The key habit is rendering pages to images and looking at them after every change, because text extraction cannot tell you about layout.

before: Give it a PDF. Get text pulled out, pages merged, split, filled, redacted or checked, with the original kept safe.
after: Do what you need to a PDF, such as pull text, merge, split, fill forms, redact or check it, while the original stays untouched. Each run gives you proof, not a promise.

before: Name a company. Get a table comparing its price multiples and key numbers with its peers.
after: Name a company. Get a table comparing its price multiples and key numbers with its peers. Bring the target company name. Use the result to plan your next step.

before: Give it your headcount plan. Get a budget by team, a month-by-month view and notes to explain gaps to finance.
after: A people budget finance will accept: headcount costs by team and cost centre, spread month by month, with notes that explain every gap. It puts HR in the same financial language as finance.

before: Give it your team and rules. Get a ranked list of people risks, owners and response steps. Not legal advice.
after: A ranked list of the people risks in your organisation, each with an owner and a response step, so nothing important sits unseen. It is a planning aid and not legal advice.

before: Pick your review cycle. Get a self-review template, a manager review draft and calibration prep with specific examples.
after: Pick your review cycle. Get a self-review template, a manager review draft and calibration prep with specific examples. Bring the review period. Use the result to plan your next step.

before: Say who you want to be known as. Get your focus, your audience and a plan to show up steadily.
after: A clear answer to who you are for, what you stand for and what you want to be known for, with a plan to show up steadily.

before: List your income and spending. Get a budget plan, such as zero-based or 50/30/20, and where money leaks.
after: A spending plan where every dollar has a job, and a clear view of where money leaks. You get either a simple 50/30/20 split or a zero-based plan where income minus spending equals zero.

before: Feed it sources. Get an Obsidian wiki that updates pages, links ideas and flags where sources disagree.
after: A personal knowledge base that grows each time you feed it a source, instead of starting over with every question. You end up with linked notes in an Obsidian vault where connections and conflicts are already marked.

before: Give it a topic in history, social science or literature. Get an activity that builds real understanding of other views.
after: A classroom activity where students work out how people actually saw their world, instead of imagining what they would feel. That difference builds sound reasoning and keeps the lesson safe and honest.

before: Name a real event or puzzle. Get a unit plan that uses several subjects to explain it.
after: Name a real event or puzzle. Get a unit plan that uses several subjects to explain it. Bring a real-world phenomenon or puzzle. Use the result to plan your next step.

before: Give it your AI app. Get traces of every step, plus tests that score answers and spot failures.
after: See every step your AI app takes, score its answers, and catch failures before users do. Phoenix is an open-source tool you run yourself, with no vendor lock-in.

before: Describe the heat or battery drain. Get safe, read-only checks run and the likely cause named.
after: Find why an Android phone runs hot or drains fast, with checks that only read and never change anything. You get the likely cause named, plus what the evidence shows and what is only a guess.

before: Say what image editing your app needs. Get Photopea embedded and scripted to open, edit and export files.
after: A working image editor inside your web page, controlled by your own code. Photopea runs in a frame, and your page can open files, run edits and export results without the user leaving your app.

before: Describe the part and its loads. Get a finite element model built, solved and plotted.
after: Describe a part and the forces or heat acting on it, and get a finite element model built, solved and plotted. It covers heat, stress and electromagnetic problems.

before: Give it a tag name or description. Get the matching PI data points found from MATLAB.
after: Give it a tag name or description. Get the matching PI data points found from MATLAB. Bring tag name, description or element name. Use the result to plan your next step.

before: Describe how orders move through your space. Get the slow steps found and a fix plan with expected time saved.
after: Find the slow steps in how orders move through your space and get a fix plan with the time each fix should save. It covers receiving an order through to leaving the door.

before: Give it a day of orders. Get groups to pick together so pickers walk less, with the expected distance saved.
after: Group a day of orders so pickers pick them together and walk less, with the expected distance saved. Fewer trips mean faster orders and lower labour cost.

before: Give it images and questions. Get a chat that describes pictures and answers questions about them.
after: A chat assistant that looks at pictures and talks about them. Ask what is in a photo, what a chart says or what a document image contains, and keep asking follow-ups.

before: Give it your deals and quota. Get pipeline cover, forecast accuracy and sales cost numbers.
after: Give it your deals and quota. Get pipeline cover, forecast accuracy and sales cost numbers. Bring deals with value, stage and age. Use the result to plan your next step.

before: Ask for a pipeline review. Get coverage, aging, conversion and at-risk deals stage by stage.
after: Ask for a pipeline review. Get coverage, aging, conversion and at-risk deals stage by stage. Bring a connected CRM. Use the result to plan your next step.

before: Give it your audience and your goal. Get a pitch or deck outline that builds belief, then asks for a clear decision.
after: A pitch or deck outline that moves your audience from attention to trust to a clear decision. It builds belief first and brings in your solution after the need is felt.

before: Say you are lost. Get the last message said again in simple words, with a little context.
after: When a reply loses you, say so and get the last message said again in plain words, with a little background first. It uses Simplified Technical English, a short-sentence style built for clarity.

before: Paste a SQL query. Get what it counts, which rows it keeps and what each column means, in plain words.
after: A SQL query turned into a plain description of what it counts, which rows it keeps and what each output column means. Anyone can then check whether the query matches the question.

before: Describe the data you need. Get a working SQL query for your database type, with a note on how it runs.
after: Describe the data you want in plain words and get a working SQL query for your database, with a short note on how it runs.

before: Give it a plan. Imagine it failed in a year and get the hidden assumptions and risks found now.
after: Weak spots in a plan, found before reality finds them. Give it the plan, imagine it failed a year from now, and work back to why.

before: Give it a plan or idea. Get a tough round of questions with a suggested answer to each.
after: A tough round of questions on your plan or idea, each with a suggested answer, so you reach a shared and settled design fast. You mostly say yes or change a few answers.

before: Give it a PLL datasheet. Get a working phase-locked loop model with the right solver set.
after: A working model of a phase-locked loop chip built from its datasheet or your system targets, with the solver set up correctly. You can then check whether the loop locks fast enough and has low enough phase noise.

before: Give it two 3D scans. Get them lined up and merged, with the right method chosen and tuned.
after: Two or more 3D scans lined up into one, with the best method chosen and tuned for your data. It is useful for building a map from lidar scans or merging overlapping captures.

before: Give it a lidar file. Get it read or saved in the right format, with its point details kept.
after: Open and save 3D lidar files without guessing which function fits which format. The skill routes by file type and keeps the extra point details such as class, time and scan angle.

before: Name your country and company size. Get handbook sections, a harassment policy and a privacy policy. Not legal advice.
after: Name your country and company size. Get handbook sections, a harassment policy and a privacy policy. Not legal advice. Bring country or region. Use the result to plan your next step.

before: Give your business facts and country. Get a draft privacy policy, terms or cookie notice to send to a lawyer.
after: Give your business facts and country. Get a draft privacy policy, terms or cookie notice to send to a lawyer. Bring business description and country. Use the result to plan your next step.

before: Give it a policy gap and the current policy. Get a marked-up draft with small edits. Not legal advice.
after: Give it a policy gap and the current policy. Get a marked-up draft with small edits. Not legal advice. Bring description of the gap. Use the result to plan your next step.

before: Describe the interface. Get a built page with careful colour, layout and motion, not a stock template look.
after: Describe the interface. Get a built page with careful colour, layout and motion, not a stock template look. Bring description of the page or app. Use the result to plan your next step.

before: Say what you want from visitors. Get popup type, timing and copy that gets signups without annoying them.
after: Popups that earn signups without making visitors leave. Tell the skill what you want from visitors and it picks the type, the timing, the trigger and the words.

before: Give it monthly or quarterly reports. Get KPIs pulled out, variances to budget flagged and a summary dashboard.
after: A monthly view of how each company you back is doing against plan. Feed it the financial packs your companies send and get the key numbers pulled out and the misses flagged.

before: Give it asset returns. Get the best mix by risk and return, with an efficient frontier chart.
after: Find the mix of assets that gives the most return for the risk you accept, and see it on an efficient frontier chart. Works in MATLAB with the Financial Toolbox, which is a paid product.

before: Give it your product and rivals. Get several ways to stand apart, each with a positioning statement and a reason.
after: Five different ways to position your product, each one aimed at a gap your rivals leave open. Every idea comes with a positioning statement and the reasoning behind it.

before: Give it your shipping, returns and loyalty setup. Get a plan for what happens after checkout so customers order again.
after: Raise the chance that every order leads to the next one. Share your shipping, returns and loyalty setup and get a plan for what happens after checkout.

before: Describe the poster or artwork. Get a finished PNG or PDF design with its own clear look.
after: A finished poster or piece of art as a PNG or PDF, with a distinct look rather than a template feel. Describe what you want and the skill makes the image itself.

before: Give it your queries or schema. Get Postgres fixes for speed, indexes and security, ranked by impact.
after: Give it your queries or schema. Get Postgres fixes for speed, indexes and security, ranked by impact. Bring slow queries or SQL files. Use the result to plan your next step.

before: Share your queries or schema. Get faster Postgres with better indexes, types and settings, ranked by impact.
after: Share a slow query or a table design and get back a faster version with the reason for each change. Fixes are ranked from biggest gain to smallest.

before: Describe your data. Get a Postgres schema with the right types, keys, indexes and rules for speed and safety.
after: A Postgres schema designed for your data, with the right column types, keys, indexes and rules so it stays fast and hard to corrupt as it grows.

before: Describe your API or paste cURL commands. Get a Postman collection file that imports and runs straight away.
after: Describe your API or paste cURL commands. Get a Postman collection file that imports and runs straight away. Bring aPI description or cURL commands. Use the result to plan your next step.

before: Give it a Windows script. Get operator, quoting and error handling mistakes caught and fixed.
after: Give it a Windows script. Get operator, quoting and error handling mistakes caught and fixed. Bring your PowerShell script. Use the result to plan your next step.

before: Give it a skill. Get practice problems that rise in difficulty and vary just enough, for worksheets or homework.
after: A set of practice problems that start easy, grow harder step by step and change just enough to build real skill. Ready for worksheets, homework or tutoring.

before: Point it at your repo. Get checks for formatting, types and tests that run before every commit.
after: Checks that run on their own before every commit, so broken or messy code never reaches your repo. You point the skill at your project and it wires everything up.

before: Give it a draft and its brief. Get checks on facts, voice, structure, AI sound and search readiness.
after: A final check on a draft before it goes live, so errors are caught before readers see them. Give it the draft and the brief and get a marked list of problems with fixes.

before: Point it at your project. Get junk files, dead code and leaked secrets found and fixed before you publish.
after: A cleaner project before it goes on GitHub. The skill reads your code file by file, fixes what it can and flags what needs your decision.

before: Give it a trained model and data. Get which inputs drove each prediction and overall, with checked plots.
after: See why a trained model made its predictions: which inputs pushed each result up or down, and which matter most overall. Every plot is checked against the real model output so you can trust it.

before: Give it a data table and a target. Get the best input columns chosen, tested and delivered as a clean table.
after: Choose the columns that best predict your target, test the choice and receive a clean table ready for training. This is for MATLAB and needs a licence.

before: Describe the page or app. Get a polished design with premium type, depth and smooth motion, not a template look.
after: A page or app that looks expensive: premium type, soft depth, careful spacing and smooth motion, rather than a template look. Describe what you need and get working code.

before: Give it an outline or document. Get a polished slide deck for your audience in Marp, reveal.js or PPTX.
after: A finished slide deck made from your outline, document or meeting notes, written for the people who will watch it. Output comes as Marp, reveal.js or PPTX.

before: Say your news. Get a media list, pitch emails and a press kit outline.
after: Tell it your news and get a plan to win press coverage: who to contact, what to say and what to put in your press kit.

before: Use it when someone pushes your AI to agree or sign off. Get answers that separate evidence from pressure.
after: A way to keep your AI honest when someone pushes it to agree, sign off or hurry. It separates what the evidence shows from what the pressure demands.

before: Give it a new product idea. Get cheap tests like landing pages and pre-orders, each with a clear pass mark.
after: Give it a new product idea. Get cheap tests like landing pages and pre-orders, each with a clear pass mark. Bring product idea. Use the result to plan your next step.

before: Give it a price you are weighing. Get whether to round it, how to price add-ons, and where to place it.
after: Decide how to show a price so it sends the signal you want. Give it a price you are weighing and learn whether to round it, how to price add-ons and where to put it on the page.

before: Give it your costs and rival offers. Get a price for each product, response rules for rival discounts, and a rollout plan.
after: Give it your costs and rival offers. Get a price for each product, response rules for rival discounts, and a rollout plan. Bring product costs and fees. Use the result to plan your next step.

before: Give it your product and prices. Get a tier and anchor layout that makes value clear without tricks.
after: A layout for your prices, tiers and anchors that makes value easy to see without tricks. Give it your product and prices and get a plan that is clear and fair.

before: Get which products sell more or less as price changes, plus price points worth testing.
after: See which of your products sell more or less when price changes, and which price points are worth testing. It reads your Shopify store data and changes nothing.

before: Give it your costs and sales data. Get the best price to try, three outcome cases, and a test you can undo.
after: The best price to try next, with three outcome cases and a test you can undo. Give it your costs and sales history and it shows what the numbers can and cannot tell you.

before: Give it your product and price survey data. Get a pricing model, price points and good, better, best tiers.
after: Choose how to charge, what to charge and how to package it. Give it your product and price survey answers and get a pricing model, a price range and good, better, best tiers.

before: Describe your product and buyers. Get tiers, a value metric and a test plan for your prices.
after: Describe your product and buyers. Get tiers, a value metric and a test plan for your prices. Bring product and target market. Use the result to plan your next step.

before: Give it a topic and sources. Get a full lesson where learners investigate a historical question from documents.
after: A full history lesson where learners investigate a real question using original documents, then argue from the evidence. Give it a topic and sources and it builds the lesson.

before: Describe your backlog and team. Get the best way to rank it from nine methods, with the steps to use it.
after: Pick the right way to rank your backlog from nine proven methods, then get the steps to use it. Describe your list and team and the skill matches a method to your situation.

before: Describe the data your app collects. Get privacy controls designed in: less data kept, clear consent, safe storage.
after: Build privacy in from day one. Describe the data your app collects and get a design that keeps less, asks for clear consent and stores data safely.

before: Describe a new feature that uses personal data. Get a privacy impact assessment with conditions and owners. First check, not legal advice.
after: A privacy impact assessment for a new feature that uses personal data, with conditions, named owners and a route to sign-off. It is a first check, not legal advice.

before: Describe how you handle personal data. Get gaps against ISO 27701, a privacy control list and an audit plan.
after: A clear view of where your handling of personal data falls short of ISO 27701, with the controls you need and a plan to audit them.

before: Describe your business and data use. Get privacy policy wording and a review checklist. Have a lawyer check it.
after: Describe your business and data use. Get privacy policy wording and a review checklist. Have a lawyer check it. Bring business and product description. Use the result to plan your next step.

before: Describe a data plan. Get where your privacy policy no longer matches, with fix wording. Not legal advice.
after: Find the places where your privacy policy no longer matches what your team actually does, with fix wording ready. It is a first check, not legal advice.

before: Describe how work gets done. Get a flowchart, who does what, and a written procedure with the edge cases.
after: A written procedure your team can follow without asking the person who knows it. It covers why the process exists, what is in and out of scope, who does each step, and what to do when things go wrong.

before: Describe a business process. Get a swim-lane map, cycle times and the one stage holding everything up.
after: The one stage that holds your process back, named and ranked, with a likely cause. Most elapsed time in a process is waiting, not work.

before: Say which product facts matter. Get fields for material, specs and sizing filled in, so AI can match products. Changes live data.
after: Product fields for material, key features, care, fit and specs, set up and filled across your Shopify catalog. AI shopping tools filter on structured facts.

before: Give it a white-background product photo. Get it placed in a real-looking scene with matching light. Your image model draws it.
after: Your plain white-background product photo placed into a believable room, desk or outdoor scene. The product stays exactly as it is. Only the surroundings change.

before: Give it your catalog. Get every product matched to a standard Shopify category, so AI can place it. Updates live products.
after: Every product in your Shopify catalog matched to the right standard category. AI shopping tools turn a request like "office chair" into a category, then pull products from it.

before: Answer questions about your product. Get one context file every marketing skill reads first.
after: One short file about your product that every other marketing task reads first, so you stop repeating yourself. It holds what you sell, who buys it, how you are positioned, and how your brand sounds.

before: Find products missing barcode, SKU, vendor or weight. Get the gaps filled so AI can quote exact items. Updates live products.
after: Missing barcodes, SKUs, vendors, product types and weights found and filled, so AI tools can quote an exact in-stock item. When this data is blank, a shopping agent cannot confirm the product is the one asked for and picks a rival with full data.

before: Give it a product idea. Get the pain points, objections and buying signals people post, with links. Collects data from websites.
after: Proof of whether people want what you plan to build, in their own words, with links. You see the complaints, workarounds, objections and "is there a tool for this" posts that repeat across Reddit, TikTok and YouTube comments.

before: Give it screenshots or a page. Get a short demo video or GIF that walks through the product.
after: A short demo video or GIF that walks someone through your product, built from screenshots or scene notes. It is planned like a small film, with a story, pacing and a clear point for every frame.

before: Point it at thin product descriptions. Get fact-rich rewrites with materials, uses and shopper words. Updates live product pages.
after: Thin product descriptions turned into copy with real facts in it. An AI shopping tool quotes your description to explain why a product fits. A one-liner gives it nothing to quote, so it moves on.

before: Give it your product facts. Get a description with the right number of claims, units and tone to lift sales.
after: A product description built on the choices that change buying decisions: how many claims to make, which units to use, and what tone fits. The rules matter more than clever adjectives.

before: Give it a product photo and selling points. Get detail page pictures with the text built in. Your image model draws them.
after: Product detail page images with the selling points already laid out as text on the picture, ready to upload. Most image models scramble written text, so the model you pick matters more than any other setting.

before: Give it an idea to test. Get a clear hypothesis, sample size, test plan and how to read the result.
after: A test plan you can run and trust: a clear hypothesis, the right sample size, and rules for when to stop and how to read the result.

before: Pick products and a custom field value. Get it set or removed on all of them. Overwrites live store data.
after: A custom field value set or cleared on every product that matches your filter, in one run instead of hundreds of manual edits. Typical fields include material, care notes and specs.

before: Describe a problem. Get ideas explored, assumptions challenged and the strongest options narrowed down.
after: A sparring partner for the early stage of an idea, before you write a spec. It pushes back, asks the hard questions and stops you settling on the first answer.

before: Point it at your product images. Get alt text set on each, so AI knows what they show. Changes live files.
after: Clear alt text on every product image, so AI tools know what each one shows. Shopping agents cannot see pixels. They read the alt text to judge color, material and style, and a file name like IMG2931 tells them nothing.

before: Describe what you are launching. Get a launch plan with timing, channels and announcement copy.
after: A launch plan with dates, channels and announcement copy, so a new product or feature gets noticed instead of slipping out quietly. Launches are treated as repeating events, not one big day.

before: Pick products and a status. Get them moved between draft, live and archived. Changes what shoppers can see and buy.
after: Pick products and a status. Get them moved between draft, live and archived. Changes what shoppers can see and buy. Bring your store domain. Use the result to plan your next step.

before: Give it failure or test data. Get life curves, failure rates and confidence ranges, worked out in MATLAB.
after: Life curves, failure rates and confidence ranges for a product, worked out from your test or field data in MATLAB. You learn how long things last and how sure you can be.

before: Give it your product facts. Get a title, bullets and description built for the marketplace you sell on.
after: Give it your product facts. Get a title, bullets and description built for the marketplace you sell on. Bring product specs and features. Use the result to plan your next step.

before: Give it your resume and a target job. Get a review against ten best practices and a version tailored to the role.
after: A PM resume reviewed line by line against ten best practices, with suggestions taken straight from your own bullet points. If you add a job posting, the feedback and rewrite are tuned to that role.

before: Say your product stage. Get the KPIs to track, a dashboard layout and how to read retention and adoption.
after: A short list of the numbers worth tracking at your product's stage, laid out as a dashboard, plus a way to read retention and adoption.

before: Give it your product numbers. Get trends against targets, what moved and what to do about it.
after: A metrics review that says what moved, why it may have moved, and what to do about it. You get a scorecard against targets instead of a pile of numbers.

before: Describe your product and buyers. Get five memorable name ideas, each with the reason it fits.
after: Five product names that fit your brand and buyers, each with the reason it works. You compare real options side by side instead of staring at a blank page.

before: Give it a product page. Get ranked changes to variants, social proof, buttons and price, each with the research behind it.
after: A ranked list of changes for a product page, each with the research behind it and the effect to expect. Layout, counts and choice design shape how much a product feels wanted and worth its price before anyone reads the copy.

before: Give it a spreadsheet of products. Get one matching photo per product, with a cost limit. Your image model draws them.
after: One matching product photo for every row in your product spreadsheet, so a whole catalog looks like a single shoot. The hard part is keeping a big set consistent, so the style rules never change and only the product details do.

before: Give it a phone photo of a product. Get a cleaner listing photo with fewer wrinkles. Your image model edits it.
after: Give it a phone photo of a product. Get a cleaner listing photo with fewer wrinkles. Your image model edits it. Bring a phone photo of the product. Use the result to plan your next step.

before: Give it one product photo. Get a full set of new angles and scenes. Your image model draws them.
after: A full set of product images from a single photo, with new angles, scenes and framing that still look like the same item. Marketplace listings often need five or more images, and detail pages need many more.

before: Give it a main product photo. Get a 3 to 5 second video for your listing. Your video model makes it.
after: A 3 to 5 second video for the video slot on your listing, made from a main product photo you already have. Many stores leave that slot empty because filming feels like too much work.

before: Describe your product and its rivals. Get the best market to compete in and a clear line on why you win.
after: The market you should compete in and one clear line on why you win there. It stops you from being compared in the wrong category.

before: Give it revenue and costs by product. Get each product's margin and which ones lose money.
after: Give it revenue and costs by product. Get each product's margin and which ones lose money. Bring revenue by product or segment. Use the result to plan your next step.

before: Describe a product or feature. Get a short product requirements document with goal, audience, value and release plan.
after: A short product requirements document your team can read in a few minutes and start work from. It is built to help people decide, not to fill pages.

before: Tell it your product. Get a shot list for photos and video, with a reason for each shot.
after: A shot list for photos and video where every shot has a reason behind it. Instead of taste, the brief follows findings on what moves sales and willingness to pay.

before: Describe your product. Get a nine-part strategy: vision, customers, trade-offs, metrics and what keeps you ahead.
after: A nine-part product strategy that shows how you will compete, win and grow. It puts vision, customers, costs, value, trade-offs, metrics, growth, skills and defensibility on one page.

before: Pick products and a tag. Get it added or removed on all of them. Changes your live catalog; preview first.
after: A tag added or removed on every product in a collection, tag group or search result, in one run. Campaign setup and teardown no longer mean editing products one at a time.

before: Describe your product team. Get a plan for finding what to build, testing ideas first and working with empowered teams.
after: A plan to move your product team from building a roadmap of features to finding what customers actually want. It helps teams own problems rather than just ship a list.

before: Give it your product list. Get tidy, consistent titles as a CSV for Shopify, plus a before and after sheet.
after: Messy Shopify product titles tidied into one pattern across the catalog, delivered as a CSV you can import as is. Only titles that need a change are in the file, so a clean store with 40 edits is better than 250 pointless ones.

before: Give it your product and screen. Get an interface built from your own design system, with every state covered.
after: An interface for your product that looks like your product, not a generic template. It is built from your existing components, spacing and type, with every state covered.

before: Give it your selling points. Get a shot script and a 15 to 30 second captioned ad. Your video model makes it.
after: A 15 to 30 second ad with a shot script, built shot by shot and joined with captions. If one shot fails, only that shot gets redone.

before: Give it your product and team. Get a vision, quarterly plan and a goal cascade for each team.
after: A product vision, a quarterly plan and a chain of goals from company down to each team, all pointing the same way. You also see how well the goals line up.

before: Give it demand and what you can make. Get your bottlenecks and a plan to close the gap.
after: Know whether your plant, warehouse or team can handle next quarter's demand before you promise it. You get a clear view of where the squeeze is, which resource limits everything else, and what it would cost to close the gap.

before: Give it standard and actual production costs. Get the gap split into price, volume and efficiency causes.
after: When actual production costs miss the standard, you need to know why. A variance report splits the gap into price, usage, labour rate and labour efficiency, so you can see which part is a purchasing issue and which is a shop floor issue.

before: Ask about recent errors. Get the Sentry issues and events summed up with the key details.
after: Ask what broke in production and get a short, readable answer pulled straight from Sentry. No clicking through dashboards to find the issues that matter.

before: Give it your sales forecast and capacity. Get a week-by-week plan of what to make and when.
after: A week-by-week plan that says what to make, how many and when. You can promise delivery dates with confidence. It balances your sales forecast and customer orders against what your capacity can really build.

before: Give it your jobs, machines and due dates. Get a job order that meets deadlines and keeps machines busy.
after: Put your jobs in the right order on the right machines so orders ship on time and no machine sits idle. You get a concrete schedule instead of a guess.

before: Give it a service. Get weak spots found and fixes like timeouts, retries and circuit breakers, so outages stay small.
after: Find the places where your service will fall over in production, and fix them before an outage spreads. The review turns vague worry into a list of weak spots with specific fixes.

before: Give it a topic. Get a project brief with a driving question, milestones and marking criteria.
after: A student-ready project brief for a unit of work, built around one driving question that gives the whole project a purpose. Teachers get a plan they can hand out and mark against.

before: Give it a project's budget, schedule and spend. Get cost and schedule indexes and a finish cost estimate.
after: A clear answer to whether your project is on budget and on time, plus a forecast of what it will cost at the end. It replaces gut feel with three numbers you can defend in a meeting.

before: Talk through your project's terms. Get a glossary and decision records so everyone uses the same words.
after: One shared set of words for your project, written down as you talk, so people stop meaning different things by the same term. It also keeps short records of why you made key decisions.

before: Describe your project. Get a one-page brief with goal, audience, tone and limits that your team can sign off.
after: A one-page brief your team can sign off before work starts, so a designer, developer or AI agent knows what to build. It turns "we want a website" into something concrete.

before: Give it a bloated project notes file. Get a lean version, plus a way for your AI to save lasting facts.
after: A short project notes file that your AI actually reads, plus a way for it to save lasting facts without piling clutter back in. Repeated corrections stop being forgotten.

before: Work on a codebase. Get a notes folder of decisions, design and rules that any AI can read later.
after: A folder of plain notes inside your project that records what it is, why choices were made and how code should be written. Any AI that can read files can pick it up later.

before: Point it at your project. Get small context files per folder so your AI reads less and costs less.
after: Small context files for each folder in your project, so your AI reads only what it needs and your token bill drops. It stops re-reading the whole project on every prompt.

before: Give it your projects. Get risks scored, resources balanced and a clear status for stakeholders.
after: A clear picture across all your projects: which risks cost the most, where people are overloaded and which projects need attention first. You end with a status report leaders can read in two minutes.

before: Point it at a project. Get a short list of skills worth adding or updating, based on how you really work.
after: A short list of skills worth adding to your project, picked from how you really work rather than a generic wish list. Updating an existing skill comes before inventing a new one.

before: Say how many codes you need and what they give. Get unique single-use discount codes made live in your store.
after: Hundreds of unique discount codes, created live in your Shopify store in one run. Each code works once, so you can hand one to each person and know who used it.

before: Give it past promotions and stock. Get a promo calendar with expected sales lift and the extra stock to have ready.
after: A promotion calendar that shows what to run and when. It shows how much extra each deal should sell and how much stock to have ready.

before: Say what you want to launch or clear. Get a gift, bundle or pre-order promotion that avoids plain price cuts.
after: A promotion that gets sales without teaching customers to wait for a markdown. You get a clear pick between a gift, bundle, pre-order incentive or limited offer, with the wording to match.

before: Point it at your AI app's inputs. Get a small filter that flags tricks and hidden instructions before they land.
after: A small filter that checks text before it reaches your AI app and flags tricks like "ignore previous instructions" or commands hidden inside documents. Bad input gets caught before it does damage.

before: Keep prompts in production. Get versioning, tests of changes, a registry and safe rollbacks.
after: Treat your prompts like code: saved, versioned, tested and safe to roll back. A wording tweak that quietly breaks a feature gets caught before users see it.

before: Give it a prompt change and a fixed set of cases. Get a clear report of what got better or worse.
after: A fair test of whether your new prompt is better than the old one. You get case-by-case evidence, so a change ships on proof, not a hunch.

before: Give it a prompt that gives weak or uneven answers. Get a tighter version that works more reliably.
after: A prompt that stops giving vague, wrong or uneven answers. You hand over the weak one and get back a tighter version that behaves the same way run after run.

before: Give it a rough prompt. Get it rebuilt into a clear, structured prompt using a fitting framework.
after: Turn a rough request like "help me code Python" into a clear, structured prompt you can paste straight into any AI. No prompting jargon needed.

before: Describe your AI app. Get a threat map and fixes against hidden instructions in text it reads.
after: A threat map and a fix list for your AI app, so text it reads cannot take it over. You see exactly where hidden instructions could get in and what they could reach.

before: Give it a task. Get lessons where students compare vague and clear prompts and see why detail changes the result.
after: A short sequence of lessons where students see for themselves why a detailed prompt beats a vague one. They stop treating AI as a magic box and start asking better questions.

before: Give it a prompt and test cases. Get scores for each version and a better prompt backed by results.
after: A prompt improved by results, not opinion. You get scores for each version against your test cases, so you can see which edits helped and by how much.

before: Give it a buyer request. Get a requirement gap score, a rival feature table and a trial plan.
