after: Before you answer a buyer's request, see how well you fit it, where you fall short and how to run a trial that wins the deal.

before: Give it text. Get grammar, spelling, punctuation and style fixed against your style guide.
after: Clean text with every fix explained, so you can send it with confidence and see what changed. It follows your chosen style guide instead of guessing.

before: Describe your ideal customer. Get a qualified list of accounts and the reason each one fits.
after: A list of accounts that really fit your ideal customer, with the reason each one made the cut. You can start outreach without sorting through junk contacts.

before: Name a prospect. Get a short personal email or sequence saved as a draft for you to review. You send it.
after: A short, personal email or multi-step sequence for one prospect, saved as a draft so you can review it before anything is sent. You stay in control of the send button.

before: Give it a working prototype. Get tests, cleaner structure and a plan to make it ready for real users.
after: A step-by-step path from a prototype that works but scares you to a product you can ship. It starts with a safety net of tests, so each later change is safe to make.

before: Name the fact you need and the database. Get it retrieved the same way every time, with source and date.
after: A fact pulled from a named public database, with the source, query and date attached. Anyone can repeat the lookup and get the same answer.

before: Paste your store reviews. Get a specific reply to each, with risky ones flagged and no refunds promised.
after: A reply for every review you paste, ready to post. Each reads as if you wrote it to that one customer, and none promise anything you have not approved.

before: Commit your branch. Get a clear pull request that says what changed, why, and what reviewers should check.
after: A pull request description that tells the reviewer what changed, why, and what to look at first. It is written from your actual committed changes, not from memory.

before: Give it a pull request. Get issues ranked by severity, security notes and clear review comments.
after: A review of a pull request that tells you what could break, what is unsafe and what to fix first. Findings come ranked, with comments you can paste straight into the review.

before: Point it at a pull request. Get complexity and risk scored, code smells flagged and review comments written.
after: A quick score for how risky and complex a pull request is, with code smells flagged and review comments already written. You know where to look before reading line by line.

before: Give it your changes. Get a clear pull request description a reviewer can follow.
after: A pull request body built for fast review: one picture of the change, proof it works, and a plain warning about how risky the merge is.

before: Give it sales and stock numbers. Get what to reorder and when, draft orders and slow movers to clear.
after: A reorder list that tells you what to buy, how much and when, based on what is actually selling. It also shows the cash stuck in stock you should not buy more of.

before: Give it your data. Get a clean Matplotlib chart, static, animated or interactive, ready to save as an image.
after: A clean chart from your data, saved as an image or built as an animated or interactive plot. You get tidy labels, sensible colours and the right chart for the numbers.

before: Give it a vision model repo on GitHub. Get a MATLAB function that runs it on your images.
after: Give it a vision model repo on GitHub. Get a MATLAB function that runs it on your images. Bring gitHub link or package name of the vision model. Use the result to plan your next step.

before: Paste your user stories. Get test scenarios with starting state, steps and the result to expect.
after: A set of test scenarios you can hand straight to a tester, one per user story. Each one says what is being checked, what must be true before you start, who does it, the steps, and what you should see after each step.

before: Name a customer. Get a health read with risk signs, value delivered and an agenda for the review.
after: Name a customer and get a plain read on how healthy the account is, plus a prep brief for the quarterly business review. The brief shows risk signs, the value you delivered, and a proposed agenda for the meeting.

before: Answer a few questions. Get a written quality bar for your project and a watch for anyone lowering it.
after: A short written quality bar for your project, with real numbers, saved in a file the whole team and any AI agent can check. It ends the argument about what good enough to ship means.

before: Give it your defect data. Get control charts, the biggest causes ranked, and a plan to cut defects.
after: A quality plan built from your own defect data. You see control charts that show whether your process is stable, a ranked list of the biggest causes of defects, and a step-by-step plan to cut them.

before: Describe a quantum system. Get a simulation with stated assumptions and checks that the numbers have settled.
after: Describe a quantum system. Get a simulation with stated assumptions and checks that the numbers have settled. Bring description of the quantum system. Use the result to plan your next step.

before: Give it your backlog and requests. Get a multi-quarter roadmap that balances build, improve and maintain, plus a not-doing list.
after: A multi-quarter roadmap you can defend in a room, plus the ranking work behind it. It balances new builds, improvements and upkeep, and ends with a list of things you are not doing and why.

before: Tell it who you need answers from. Get a questionnaire aimed at what they know and you do not.
after: When you need answers only one person has, you get a ready document to send them. It is built so they can reply on their own time, or you can fill it in together in a meeting.

before: Describe a process with queues and limited resources. Get a simulation with repeated runs and a clear summary of results.
after: Find out how a system with waiting lines will behave before you build it or change it. You get a simulation with repeated runs and a clear summary, such as average wait, how busy each resource is, and how much the results vary.

before: Ask a quick question, like using customer logos. Get fine, needs a look or hold, with a reason. Not legal advice.
after: A one-minute answer to a quick legal question: fine, needs a look, or hold. You get one sentence of reasoning and, if it is not fine, the next step.

before: Give it a CSV of past values. Get a forecast with ranges and a test on held-back data, with no model training.
after: A forecast of your numbers with ranges around it, tested against data you held back, and no model training. You give it a CSV of past values and see how well it would have predicted what you already know.

before: Paste your quiz results or LMS numbers. Get what they say and what to do in class next.
after: Your quiz results or LMS numbers turned into a plain statement of what is going on, and what to do in class next. It helps you avoid acting on a number that means less than it looks.

before: Describe who you want to sort. Get quiz questions, scoring, result groups and matching recommendations that can capture leads.
after: A quiz that sorts people into useful groups and points each group to the right product, plus a way to capture their email. It is built to produce leads, not just clicks.

before: Describe your audience. Get a scored quiz that sorts people, captures leads and leads into the right next offer.
after: A scored quiz that draws in the right people, sorts them by result, and sends each one to the offer that fits. Visitors leave with a score and you leave with their answers and contact details.

before: Give it your call notes, photos or an RFP. Get a branded, costed proposal or quote in your own template.
after: Notes from a call, photos of a job, or an RFP become a branded, priced proposal ready to send. It uses your own templates and past prices, so quotes look the same each time and stop eating your evenings.

before: Give it a radar datasheet. Get a simulated scene, fixes for missed detections and result plots.
after: A simulated radar scene built from your datasheet, with the detections it produces, plots, and fixes if some targets are missed. You can trust the result because it is checked against a hand calculation of what the radar should see.

before: Give it radar or sonar needs. Get a chosen waveform, its settings and plots of how well it performs.
after: A radar or sonar waveform chosen for your needs, with its settings and plots showing how well it works. You see range resolution, sidelobes and how it copes with moving targets.

before: Give it a test signal. Get it sent over the air and the received IQ data captured.
after: A test signal sent over the air from a software defined radio, and the received IQ data captured and ready to study. You can run a loopback test, capture a band, or send for a long time.

before: Describe your documents. Get chunking, embedding and vector database choices, with ways to test results.
after: A design for retrieving answers from your documents, backed by numbers from your own files rather than guesses. You get chunking, embedding and vector database choices, plus a test that shows how well retrieval works.

before: Connect Ahrefs. Get the keywords worth tracking, grouped by purpose, with baselines, alert limits and a reporting routine.
after: A rank tracking setup you can start using today. It picks the keywords worth watching, groups them by purpose, records where you stand now, and sets the points at which you should be alerted.

before: Name a region. Get a dashboard of key indicators, the yield curve and what they say about the cycle.
after: Name a region. Get a dashboard of key indicators, the yield curve and what they say about the cycle. Bring region to cover (India by default). Use the result to plan your next step.

before: Describe your product. Get a style guide for a raw, blunt look, with type, colour, states and checks.
after: A style guide for a raw, blunt, anti-polish look, ready for designers and developers to build from. It covers type, colour, spacing, states and checks, so the harsh look stays consistent and still works for people.

before: Describe the screen. Get React and Next.js components with fast loading, Tailwind styling and bundle checks.
after: React and Next.js components for the screen you describe, written in TypeScript with Tailwind styling, and checked for load speed and bundle size. You get code you can drop into a project.

before: Point it at a React or React Native app. Get a clear folder layout and rules for what may import what.
after: A clear folder layout for your React or React Native app, plus simple rules for what may import what. Any contributor can then answer where code lives without asking anyone.

before: Describe your product. Get a landing page as React code with hero, pricing, FAQ and proof sections.
after: A full landing page as React code, built from your product description. It has a hero, features, pricing, FAQ and proof sections, each with copy written to a proven pattern.

before: Point it at your React app. Get unit, integration and end-to-end tests for the parts that lack them.
after: Tests for the parts of your React app that have none: unit tests for components, integration tests, and end-to-end tests for key routes. You also learn where your coverage falls short.

before: Give it code. Get clearer names, smaller functions and tidier error handling, each with a reason. Uses Clean Code.
after: Your code reviewed for how easily a stranger can read it, with a score out of 10 and clear fixes. Each suggestion comes with the reason behind it, based on the Clean Code approach.

before: Paste a text. Get the reading strategies that fit its hard parts, in a teaching order.
after: For a given text, you get the reading strategies that fit its hard parts, in the order to teach them. This helps students who stall on a passage and need support aimed at the real barrier.

before: Answer a few quick questions at a time. Get a README and short decision records that hold your plans.
after: Your project vision and decisions captured in a README and short decision records, written from a quick interview. You answer a few questions at a time, and your taste and reasoning end up saved as plain text.

before: Point it at a project. Get each README step marked working or broken, with proof, and the edits that fix it.
after: Each step in your README marked working, broken, missing or unchecked, with proof from the repo and the edits that fix it. You see what a new user would hit first.

before: Give it a strategy. Get an honest diagnosis, a guiding policy and coherent actions, or a list of what is hollow.
after: An honest check of your strategy, telling you whether it is a real plan or a list of goals. If it is thin, you get a rebuilt version with a diagnosis, a guiding policy and actions that fit together.

before: Say why your brand must change. Get what to keep, what to change and a rollout plan.
after: A rebrand plan that says what to keep, what to change and how to roll it out without losing customer trust. It begins with the real reason for the change, since a new logo alone never fixes a strategy problem.

before: Write what you remember and rate your confidence first. Your AI then fills gaps instead of repeating what you know.
after: A study helper that makes you try first. You write what you remember and rate how sure you are, and only then does your AI fill the gaps.

before: Give it a topic. Get a cited briefing of what Reddit, Hacker News and the web say lately. Collects data from websites.
after: A cited briefing on what people have said lately about a topic, drawn from Reddit, Hacker News and the open web. X is an option if you supply an export.

before: Give it a break from a reconciliation. Get it traced to its source entries on both sides, and what differs.
after: A break in your reconciliation traced back to the entries that caused it, on both sides, with the differing detail named. You get a one-sentence root cause, an owner and a next action.

before: Give it audio or video. Get the words written out, with each speaker labelled.
after: Your audio or video turned into written words, with each speaker labelled if you want. You get a clean text file or structured data you can search, quote or summarise.

before: Describe the report you want in plain words. Get the numbers pulled, a workbook, and a saved report to rerun.
after: Describe a report once in your own words and get the numbers pulled, a chat summary and an Excel workbook. The report definition is saved, so you can rerun it next week with one phrase.

before: Give it a topic or subreddit. Get posts and comments in a table you can study. Collects data from websites.
after: Reddit posts and comments in a table you can sort and study, without needing a Reddit API key. Ask for a topic, a subreddit or a user, and get structured rows back.

before: Get redirects that chain from one to another or share a target, so shoppers and search get there fast.
after: Get redirects that chain from one to another or share a target, so shoppers and search get there fast. Bring store domain. Use the result to plan your next step.

before: Give it a role. Get fair reference questions, a call script and a sheet to record answers. Check local rules first.
after: A fair, consistent reference check for a role: a question set, a call script, and a sheet to record answers. Every candidate gets the same questions, so you can compare references on the same footing.

before: Describe your product. Get a referral or affiliate program with rewards, flow and launch plan.
after: A referral or affiliate program designed for your product, with the rewards, the sign-up flow and a launch plan. You can see how the numbers would work before you spend on it.

before: Name the order and items. Get a full or partial refund, plus a replacement order if you want one. Moves real money.
after: A refund issued on the right order, for the right items, with a replacement draft order ready if the customer wants one. No clicking through the Shopify admin, and no guessing at amounts.

before: Pick products, collections or dates. Get refund rates that point to quality or listing problems.
after: Which products get sent back most? This gives you a refund rate for each product, vendor or time period, so you can see where quality or listing problems hide.

before: Get the average days from return request to refund, and the returns that ran late.
after: The average number of days between a return request and the refund, plus a list of the returns that took too long. It shows whether you keep the promise you make to customers.

before: Give it a data table. Get a fitted regression or time series model with checks and a plain read of the results.
after: A fitted model for your data table, with the checks that show whether you can trust it, and a plain reading of what the numbers mean.

before: Point it at your commits. Get tidy release notes and the right version bump from Conventional Commits.
after: Release notes written from your commit history, with the right version bump worked out for you. Raw git messages turn into a changelog that people can actually read.

before: Point it at your project. Get the version bumped, a changelog written and a tagged release ready to publish.
after: Everything needed to ship a version in one pass: the number bumped, the changelog written and a tagged release ready to publish. You skip the manual file editing that people forget.

before: Point it at a deployed service. Get fresh proof across code, CI, database and live routes before you call it ready.
after: A clear pass, fail or blocked verdict on a deployed service, backed by fresh evidence instead of a green build light. A finished pipeline does not mean the live site works, and this shows the difference.

before: Point it at a release. Get a read-only report of real deploy risks: migrations, config, order and rollback.
after: A short report listing the real reasons a release could fail on deploy. You find the missing migration, the absent setting or the wrong rollout order before users do.

before: Name your service. Get service level targets, error budgets and alerts to track them.
after: Name your service. Get service level targets, error budgets and alerts to track them. Bring name and type of your service. Use the result to plan your next step.

before: Point it at your project. Get it deployed on Render, with a setup file and the link.
after: Your project live on Render, with the setup file written and the dashboard link in your hand. You do not need to learn the hosting settings first.

before: Ask what is renewing. Get upcoming renewals with timing, risk and room to raise the price.
after: A list of renewals coming up, sorted by timing and risk, with a read on how much room you have to raise the price. A renewal you plan at ninety days out is a conversation.

before: Say what you need to train. Get a rented GPU server chosen, set up, loaded with your files and shut down after.
after: A rented GPU machine picked for your job, set up, loaded with your files and shut down when you finish. You stop paying for idle hardware.

before: Get a sales forecast for each product, plus when to reorder and how many to buy.
after: For every product, a sales forecast, the stock level at which to reorder, and how many units to buy. It tells you what runs out before the next delivery lands.

before: Get the share of customers who order again within your chosen days, split by product or collection.
after: The share of your customers who come back and order again within the number of days you pick, with the rate split by first product bought.

before: Get orders with many partial refunds or high refund share, a sign of fraud, complaints or process gaps.
after: Orders that look odd: several small refunds on one order, or a large share of the total refunded. These can point to fraud, a product complaint or a gap in how you handle returns.

before: Name a repeat task. Get exact steps, fixes if it fails, how to roll back and who to call.
after: A step-by-step guide for a task someone has to run again and again, written so a person on call can follow it at 2am. What lives in one person's head ends up on the page.

before: Describe a recurring job. Get a loop with triggers, checks, stop rules and handoffs.
after: Describe a recurring job. Get a loop with triggers, checks, stop rules and handoffs. Bring what you want done repeatedly. Use the result to plan your next step.

before: Describe your business. Get a growth plan with a forecast, built step by step from your marketing to your numbers.
after: A growth plan and forecast for a business whose good months happened by luck, built one phase at a time. Each phase produces a document that the next phase uses.

before: Point it at your screen history. Get a list of tasks you repeat and draft skills to automate them.
after: A list of tasks you do again and again, with draft skills ready to automate them. It finds the patterns in your own screen history that you stopped noticing.

before: Point it at a repo. Get a slide deck with cited facts that warns you when the code changes.
after: A slide deck about your code where every fact points to a file and line, and a check that tells you when the slides no longer match.

before: Give it your data. Get a clear report with charts, such as a sprint retro, financial summary or postmortem.
after: A finished report from your raw numbers, with the charts and written insights already in place. A sprint retro, a financial summary or an incident postmortem no longer starts from a blank page.

before: Give it your margins and stock. Get safe automatic price rules, test cases, and a kill switch you can trust.
after: A set of price rules that change your prices on their own within safe limits, with test cases and a stop button. You get dynamic pricing without a price war or a sale below cost.

before: Give it a loose request. Get a few rounds of sharp questions first, so the first draft lands.
after: Better first drafts, because the AI asks sharp questions before it starts. A loose request like "write me a plan" gets turned into clear choices about scope, audience, tone and format.

before: Give it a vague request. Get the few questions that matter, with default answers, before any work starts.
after: The handful of questions that matter before work begins, each with a default answer so you can reply with one word. It stops wrong work before it starts.

before: Give it a vague research need. Get one clear paragraph a deep-research tool can act on without questions.
after: One clear paragraph that a deep research tool can act on without asking you anything. Vague research needs usually give vague answers, and this fixes the request before you send it.

before: Name the funder and your idea. Get aims, a compliance checklist, a budget outline and a critique of your draft.
after: A grant application taking shape: aims, a checklist of the funder's rules, a budget outline and a critique of your draft. You find gaps before reviewers do.

before: Describe what you observed. Get testable hypotheses, rival explanations, predictions and a plan to test them.
after: Testable explanations for something you observed, with rival explanations, predictions that tell them apart and a plan to test them. It keeps you from falling for the first story that fits.

before: Describe your field or stuck project. Get ten ways to find research ideas worth chasing, with the best ones ranked.
after: Ten different ways to find a research idea worth chasing, applied to your field, with the strongest ideas ranked at the end. When you are stuck, a fresh angle matters more than a longer list.

before: Name your research area. Get ideas built, challenged and ranked, with assumptions and a decision log.
after: A structured brainstorm for your research area that builds ideas, challenges them and ranks them, ending with a log of why you chose what you chose.

before: Give it a topic. Get a list of items to compare and questions to answer for each, found online. Scrapes sites.
after: Give it a topic. Get a list of items to compare and questions to answer for each, found online. Scrapes sites. Bring research topic. Use the result to plan your next step.

before: Give it your results or a method section. Get charts and architecture diagrams that look ready for a paper.
after: Figures that look ready for a conference paper: charts from your results and architecture diagrams from your method section. You describe the work and skip the hours in a drawing tool.

before: Give it a paper, article or report. Get the key findings, plain summaries and a comparison across sources.
after: The key findings of a paper, article or report in plain language, plus a comparison across several sources and correctly formatted citations. You read less and still know what matters.

before: Give it your findings. Get a manuscript in standard sections with checked citations and reporting rules applied.
after: A manuscript drafted in the standard sections, with citations formatted correctly and the right reporting rules applied. It turns your findings into text a journal editor can read.

before: Give it your approved text and images. Get an editable PowerPoint poster at print size, checked for access and file safety.
after: Give it your approved text and images. Get an editable PowerPoint poster at print size, checked for access and file safety. Bring approved poster text. Use the result to plan your next step.

before: Give it your results and figures. Get a printable research poster in LaTeX as a PDF.
after: A printable research poster as a PDF, built in LaTeX from your results and figures. LaTeX keeps text sharp and layouts exact, so it prints well at conference size.

before: Describe your research ideas. Get help choosing a problem worth pursuing, or why a project is stuck.
after: Help choosing a research problem worth your years, or finding out why a current project is stuck. It uses a decision tree for problem choice from a published paper by Fischbach and Walsh.

before: Give it a research question. Get a run of tested ideas, a log of what you learned, and a findings write-up.
after: A research project run from question to write-up: a series of tested ideas, a log of what you learned, and a findings report. The agent keeps going without asking you at every step.

before: Give it a question. Get a conclusion-first report with sources ranked and cross-checked.
after: A research report that opens with the conclusion, ranks every source by trust, and states what remains unknown. Readers can see how you got there and how sure you are.

before: Give it your research files. Get one report with a contents list and every checked answer. Unsure ones are left out.
after: One report that pulls together the results from many research files, with a contents list and only the answers that were checked. Uncertain values are left out instead of guessed.

before: Give it interviews, surveys or tickets. Get themes ranked by how often they come up, with quotes.
after: The themes in your interviews, surveys or support tickets, ranked by how often they come up and backed by real quotes. You stop reading piles of notes and start seeing the pattern.

before: Give it your suppliers. Get ethics and environment gaps found, a questionnaire to send, and an improvement plan.
after: Give it your suppliers. Get ethics and environment gaps found, a questionnaire to send, and an improvement plan. Bring a list of your suppliers. Use the result to plan your next step.

before: Describe what your service does. Get a clean REST API plan with routes, status codes, paging and docs.
after: A complete plan for a REST API before anyone writes code: the routes, the methods, the status codes and the docs. Mistakes caught here cost minutes.

before: Get every product below your stock limit, grouped by supplier, as a list ready to order from.
after: Get every product below your stock limit, grouped by supplier, as a list ready to order from. Bring your Shopify store address. Use the result to plan your next step.

before: Give it your sales and lead times. Get a restock rule for each product group, like min-max or fixed cycle.
after: A restock rule for each group of products, so reordering stops being a weekly guess. You get a clear trigger, an order size and a reason it fits that group's sales pattern.

before: Describe a conflict between students. Get steps to repair trust and relationships. Not legal or medical advice.
after: Describe a conflict between students. Get steps to repair trust and relationships. Not legal or medical advice. Bring what happened. Use the result to plan your next step.

before: Give it user activity data. Get retention curves by sign-up group, feature adoption trends and what they suggest.
after: A clear picture of which sign-up groups stay and which leave, with charts and a short list of what to look into next. You see where the drop-off happens and who it happens to.

before: Give it signup and activity dates. Get retention by group over time, as a colour-coded grid with a plain reading.
after: A colour-coded grid that shows, for each sign-up group, how many people come back in each following period, with a plain-language reading underneath. One glance tells you if you are keeping people better than last quarter.

before: Describe why users drop off. Get the cause found and fixes to onboarding and habits. Uses behavior design.
after: A diagnosis of why people sign up and then drift away, plus specific changes to your first-use experience. The skill treats this as a design problem, not a motivation problem, and scores your product out of 10.

before: Give it your age, savings and goals. Get a projected nest egg and the gap to your target.
after: A projected retirement pot and the exact gap between it and the amount you need. You also see the monthly saving that would close that gap.

before: Give it a topic. Get low-stakes recall questions at easy, medium and hard levels for starters or revision.
after: A set of short recall questions on one topic, ready to use as a lesson starter or revision task. Because they are low stakes, students practise pulling facts from memory, which makes them stick better than re-reading.

before: Describe your product. Get a style guide with a vintage look, nostalgic type and bold colour pairs.
after: Describe your product. Get a style guide with a vintage look, nostalgic type and bold colour pairs. Bring a description of your product. Use the result to plan your next step.

before: Get the true cost of returns by reason and product: refunds, shipping lost and written-off stock.
after: The real cost of your returns, not only the refund amount. You see what each return reason and each product costs you in refunds, lost shipping income, written-off stock and handling time.

before: Give it your deliveries and returns to collect. Get routes that bring returns back on the same trip.
after: Give it your deliveries and returns to collect. Get routes that bring returns back on the same trip. Bring delivery stops with quantities. Use the result to plan your next step.

before: Get return reasons counted by product, to find quality problems and listings that mislead.
after: Get return reasons counted by product, to find quality problems and listings that mislead. Bring your Shopify store address. Use the result to plan your next step.

before: Name the order, items and reason. Get a formal return record opened in Shopify. Creates a live return.
after: Name the order, items and reason. Get a formal return record opened in Shopify. Creates a live return. Bring the order ID. Use the result to plan your next step.

before: Get returned items added back to stock at the right location. Changes live stock, so skip damaged goods.
after: Returned items put back into available stock at the correct location, so your counts match the shelf. It changes live inventory, so it starts in preview mode and skips damaged goods.

before: Tell it your products. Get a plan to reuse, refurbish or recycle them and take back returns.
after: Tell it your products. Get a plan to reuse, refurbish or recycle them and take back returns. Bring your products and their materials. Use the result to plan your next step.

before: Run it on your orders. Get revenue for each warehouse or fulfillment location, ready for a split profit view.
after: Revenue split by the warehouse or fulfilment centre that shipped each order, so you can judge every location's profit on its own. It reads your Shopify data only and changes nothing.

before: Describe your product and users. Get three to five ways to earn from it, with risks and tests.
after: Three to five different ways your product could earn money, each with who pays, the risks and a cheap test to run first. You choose with evidence instead of gut feel.

before: Give it a customer contract. Get its promises, price split and timing of revenue under IFRS 15 or ASC 606.
after: Give it a customer contract. Get its promises, price split and timing of revenue under IFRS 15 or ASC 606. Bring the customer contract or its key terms. Use the result to plan your next step.

before: Point it at your open pull request. Get each reviewer comment handled and the code updated.
after: Every reviewer comment on your open pull request, listed and numbered, with the code changes made for the ones you pick. You stay in control of which feedback gets applied.

before: Give it a code review comment. Get a direct version that reads like a teammate wrote it.
after: Give it a code review comment. Get a direct version that reads like a teammate wrote it. Bring one or more code review comments. Use the result to plan your next step.

before: Give it your team and goals. Get review forms, goal templates and a guide for fair rating meetings. Not legal advice.
after: A ready set of performance review materials: appraisal forms, goal templates and a guide for running fair rating meetings. Managers get wording they can use instead of starting from a blank page.

before: Give it your product reviews. Get the pain points, praise and feature requests, ranked by how often they come up.
after: Your customer reviews boiled down to what people complain about, what they love and what they ask for, ranked by how often each comes up.

before: Tell it about your reviews. Get when to ask, how to word the request, and how to answer a bad review.
after: A plan for getting more reviews and replying to bad ones in a way that wins over everyone watching. It rests on a few findings that go against common habit.

before: List your topics and dates. Get a spaced revision schedule that brings each topic back at the right gaps.
after: A week-by-week revision plan that brings each topic back at gaps chosen to stop it fading from memory. You get new teaching and review slots in one table.

before: Give it S-parameter files or a spec. Get RF chains modeled, with gain, noise and stability checked.
after: A working model of your radio frequency chain, with gain, noise, distortion and stability checked, built in MATLAB from measured files or your spec. You find problems on screen before you build hardware.

before: Paste an RFP or security questionnaire. Get requirements sorted by must have, a fit score and draft answers.
after: A response plan for a tender or security questionnaire that shows what the buyer wants, where you are strong and whether to bid. It marks gaps openly and never invents claims.

before: Give it a topic. Get what is rising on Google Trends and social sites. Collects data from websites.
after: A short report on what is rising for your topic across Google Trends, Instagram, Facebook, YouTube and TikTok, so your content follows real interest. It collects public data by running web scrapers.

before: Give it an API or config design. Get the easy-to-misuse parts that lead to security mistakes.
after: Give it an API or config design. Get the easy-to-misuse parts that lead to security mistakes. Bring the API, library interface or config schema. Use the result to plan your next step.

before: Get orders Shopify marks as risky tagged for review, and held from shipping if you choose. Changes live orders.
after: Orders Shopify rates high risk are tagged for review and, if you choose, held so they cannot ship until you check them. It changes live orders, so it starts as a preview.

before: Describe your product. Get a style guide with a two-colour print look on warm paper, plus rules for each part.
after: A style guide for a two-colour print look on warm paper: bright pink, deep blue and offset shadows that feel hand printed. Your team can build pages that look like a risograph poster.

before: Connect Ahrefs and name rivals. Get keywords they rank for that you do not, ranked by opportunity into quick wins.
after: A ranked list of search terms your rivals appear for and you do not, so you know which pages to write next. Quick wins are marked, and related terms are grouped.

before: Name your site and rivals. Get a comparison of search overlap, content depth, backlinks, technical state and brand presence.
after: A side-by-side view of how your site stacks up against rivals in search, showing why they outrank you and what to do about it. You see gaps in topics, links and site health.

before: Name your top rivals. Get a side-by-side of their channels, prices and messages, plus the gaps you can win.
after: A side-by-side look at your top rivals: where they sell, what they charge and how they pitch their products, with the gaps you can step into.

before: Give it sequencing output. Get counts ready to compare gene activity between groups, with replicate and setup checks.
after: Sequencing output turned into a checked table of gene counts, ready to compare gene activity between groups. Mistakes in set-up are caught before they ruin the analysis.

before: Give it gene counts for two or more groups. Get which genes changed, with checks, corrected p-values and plots.
after: A list of genes that really changed between your groups, with corrected p-values, effect sizes and plots, from the PyDESeq2 tool in Python. Checks come first so a bad input does not give a confident wrong answer.

before: Describe the road layout. Get lanes, junctions, signs and signals built as a RoadRunner HD map.
after: A road network built from your description as a RoadRunner HD map file, with lanes, boundaries, markings, junctions, signs, signals, barriers and parking. You get a scene that can be used to test automated driving.

before: Give it a Lanelet2 map. Get a RoadRunner HD map built from it, ready for simulation.
after: A Lanelet2 map turned into a RoadRunner HD map file you can open and simulate. The whole pipeline runs, so you get a finished scene and not half a road.

before: Give it a map file. Get it loaded into RoadRunner as a driving scene you can check by eye.
after: A map file loaded into RoadRunner as a driving scene you can look over by eye, so you can see whether a conversion worked. Setup mistakes are caught before the import runs.

before: Give it your plans. Get a roadmap story, release notes or changelog written for executives, engineers or customers.
after: One set of plans can sound wrong when it reaches the wrong reader. Here you turn your roadmap into a story that fits who is reading it: a board, an engineering team or your customers.

before: Name your robot arm. Get a MATLAB model ready for moves, reach checks and drawing.
after: A MATLAB robot arm model you can trust, so later moves and reach checks do not quietly go wrong. Name the arm, such as a UR5e, KUKA iiwa or Panda, and it builds the model.

before: Give it a start and goal pose. Get a smooth path and timed moves for the arm.
after: An arm that moves from pose A to pose B along a path that avoids obstacles, with timing that respects speed and acceleration limits. That is what you finish with, as MATLAB code you can run.

before: Give it your robot data. Get a pi0 robot model fine-tuned on it, and a server that runs it.
after: Give it your robot data. Get a pi0 robot model fine-tuned on it, and a server that runs it. Bring your robot dataset. Use the result to plan your next step.

before: Give it your stock lengths and cut list. Get cutting patterns that use the fewest pieces and waste the least.
after: A cutting plan that tells you how to slice each rod, pipe or beam so you buy fewer lengths and throw away less offcut. Give it your stock lengths and the pieces you need.

before: Name your roles. Get the key skills for each, what good looks like at each level, and matching interview questions.
after: A skills framework your team can use for hiring, reviews and growth, written role by role. Name your roles and get the key skills for each, plus what good looks like at every level.

before: Paste a rule that changed. Get which of your policies it touches and what to change. First check, not legal advice.
after: Paste in a rule that just changed and see which of your own policies it touches. You get a gap list: what the rule now asks for, what your policy says and what to edit.

before: Describe a new feature or plan. Get the rules that may apply, approvals needed and risk areas. Not legal advice.
after: Describe a feature, campaign or plan before launch and get the rules that may apply, who must sign off and where the risk sits. It is a first-pass view, not legal advice.

before: Name a service. Get runbooks for deploy, incidents, maintenance and rollback, ready to edit.
after: On-call people need clear steps at 3 a.m., and this builds them before launch. Name a service and get a runbook with sections for deploy, incidents, maintenance and rollback, ready to fill in.

before: Give it a product or feature. Get a blunt review on focus, simplicity and end-to-end quality, with what to cut.
after: A blunt review of your product or feature that says what to cut and what to fix, with a score out of ten. It judges your work the way Steve Jobs ran product reviews: start with the customer, then subtract.

before: Give it a one-line SaaS idea. Get eight files: research, analysis, architecture, features, screens, phases and a step-by-step build plan.
after: Give it a one-line SaaS idea. Get eight files: research, analysis, architecture, features, screens, phases and a step-by-step build plan. Bring your idea in one line. Use the result to plan your next step.

before: Share your revenue and customers. Get your ARR, churn, CAC and LTV read, with what to fix first.
after: Know whether your subscription business is healthy, and what to fix first. Share your revenue and customer numbers and get your key figures worked out, each marked healthy, watch or critical.

before: Give it your SaaS idea. Get a stack choice, build order and launch checklist you can follow.
after: A clear route from idea to first paying customers: which tools to use, what to build in which order and what to check before going live.

before: Give it your product and customers. Get a value metric, tier layout and pricing tests to run.
after: A price page you can defend: what to charge for, how many plans to offer and which pricing tests to run next. Give it your product and your customers.

before: Describe your app. Get a Next.js project with sign-in, database, billing, API routes and a dashboard.
after: A working Next.js project for your software product with sign-in, database, payments, API routes and a dashboard already in place. You describe the app, pick your tools, and get the whole file tree.

before: Give it a software subscription contract. Get renewal traps, price rises, uptime and data terms flagged. A first check, not legal advice.
after: A subscription contract can cost far more over three renewals than in year one. Give it a software agreement and it flags the traps: auto-renewal windows, price rises, uptime promises and what happens to your data.

before: Ask a question about your Postgres data. Get a read-only query run with write protection and the results back.
after: Ask a question about your Postgres data in plain words and see real results, with no risk of changing anything. Every query runs read-only, so a bad command cannot delete or edit a row.

before: Describe your release. Get a deploy plan with checks, rollback steps and how to know it worked.
after: A deploy plan that tells you what to check before shipping, how to go back if it fails, and how to tell it worked. Describe your release and it fits the steps to where you host.

before: Get API keys and env variables checked and loaded without ever showing the values in logs or chat.
after: Check that your API keys and environment variables are set, valid and loaded, without any secret ever appearing in chat, logs or command history. The point is that Claude never sees the values.

before: Point it at your server or worker. Get code that finishes live work and exits cleanly when stopped.
after: Code that lets your server or worker stop without dropping live requests or losing half-done jobs. Point it at your service and get a shutdown routine for when it receives a stop signal.

before: Give it company facts. Get a draft sale memorandum with a clear structure and story.
after: The long document buyers read first when a company is for sale, drafted from your facts. It has to tell a clear story, and this gives it a set order and flow.

before: Describe a sale process. Get a draft letter with bid instructions, deadlines and meeting details.
after: The letter that tells bidders how your sale will run: when to bid, what to include and how to meet management. Describe the process and get a draft for an advisor to check.

before: Name your rival. Get a battlecard with comparisons, reply scripts, positioning and win themes.
after: A one-page guide your sales team can use in a live deal against a named rival. Give it the competitor and get comparisons, reply scripts and the points that win deals.

before: Get live products that are not published to the sales channels you expect.
after: A list of live products that are missing from the sales channels where you expect them. A product that is active but absent from Google Shopping, Meta or your online store earns nothing, and nobody notices the loss.

before: Pick a date range. Get revenue, units and average order value for each sales channel.
after: See which channels bring in your money: online store, point of sale, draft orders and more. Pick a date range and get revenue, units sold and average order value for each channel.

before: Name the deal or buyer. Get a pitch deck outline, one-pager, objection sheet or demo script.
after: The sales material your reps will actually open and use. Name the deal or buyer and get a pitch deck outline, a one-pager, an objection sheet or a demo script.

before: Paste your sales copy. Get a direct-response critique with fixes for the weakest parts.
after: A direct-response review of your sales copy that points to the weakest parts and shows how to fix them. Paste in a video sales letter, email, ad or landing page and get a critique grounded in the methods of well-known response copywriters.

before: Ask for your day. Get today's meetings with context, deals closing soon, waiting emails and your top actions.
after: Start your sales day knowing where to put your time. Ask for your briefing and get today's meetings with account context, deals close to closing, customer emails waiting on you and your top actions.

before: Give it your sales data. Get a 30 day plan of what to push, what offers to run and what to hold.
after: A thirty-day plan of what to promote, which offers to run and what to hold back, built from your real sales. It is a strategy brief, with no calendar and no finished posts.

before: Give it the prospect needs. Get a proposal or RFP reply with value, price, timeline and proof.
after: A proposal or RFP reply that speaks to what the buyer asked for, with value, price, timeline and proof in one document. Give it the prospect's needs and get a draft to polish.

before: Pick a filing period. Get tax collected by state, province and rate, ready for filing prep.
after: Tax collected, grouped the way you file it. Pick a period and get your sales tax split by state, province or rate, ready for whoever prepares your return.

before: Say which columns and rules you need. Get a realistic fake dataset as CSV, JSON, SQL or a script.
after: Realistic fake data for testing, in the shape and size you need. Tell it the columns and rules and get a dataset as CSV, JSON, SQL inserts or a script that makes it.

before: Say what effect you want to detect. Get how many subjects you need, with power curves you can put in a grant.
after: The number of subjects, samples or replicates your study needs, worked out before you collect any data. Say what effect you want to detect and get a sample size with power curves ready for a grant or protocol.

before: Describe your business in Saudi Arabia. Get which Saudi cyber and data rules apply, then the steps for each.
after: Operating in Saudi Arabia means several rule sets at once, and the hard part is knowing which are yours. Describe your business and get the Saudi cyber and data rules that apply, then steps for each.

before: Give it PDFs, Office files or scans. Get text with page positions, read with OCR when needed, all on your computer.
after: Text out of PDFs, Office files and scanned images, with the position of every line on the page, all processed on your own computer. Nothing goes to a cloud service.

before: Give it a cron schedule. Get a plain-English meaning, the next run times, and any silent mistakes that stop or repeat it.
after: Find out what your cron schedule will really do before it ships. Paste the expression and get a plain English meaning, the next run times and any silent mistakes that stop it or make it run too often.

before: Name the page type. Get checked JSON-LD markup ready to paste for search results.
after: Structured data for your page that search engines can read, checked and ready to paste into your site. Name the page type and give the details to get JSON-LD markup that can make your listing eligible for rich results.

before: Ask a research question. Get papers, preprints, citations and open full text from 18 free sources, with the search shown.
after: A literature search you can repeat and defend. Ask a research question and get papers, preprints, citations and open full text from eighteen free sources, with the exact queries shown so anyone can rerun them.

before: Give it a paper or thesis. Get a fair review of what is strong, what is weak and what to fix next.
after: Honest feedback on a paper, thesis, protocol or research idea, so you know what is strong, what is weak and what to fix next. The review is written in words first, with evidence for each point.

before: Name your science field and task. Get datasets, models and tools worth trying, with notes on fit.
after: A short list of datasets, models and tools for your science field and task, with notes on which are worth trying. Name your area, such as protein folding, weather or galaxy images, and the job you want done.

before: Describe a diagram. Get a draft of a network, pathway or flowchart, reviewed and refined once or twice.
after: A draft figure of your network, pathway or flowchart, saved as a PNG you can check label by label. You describe the parts and how they connect in plain words, and an image model draws the first version.

before: Give it your results and notes. Get manuscript sections with sources tracked, guideline gaps flagged and references checked.
after: Manuscript sections you can trust because every claim points back to something you supplied. You hand over results, notes and sources, and get Introduction, Methods, Results or Discussion drafts in clear scientific prose.

before: Name a research topic. Get papers and pages found by meaning, with text pulled out of the links. Uses Exa.
after: Name a research topic. Get papers and pages found by meaning, with text pulled out of the links. Uses Exa. Bring a research topic or question. Use the result to plan your next step.

before: Ask for a screen, a window or a part of one. Get a saved screenshot.
after: A saved screenshot of exactly what you asked for: the whole desktop, one app window, or a region of the screen. Say where to save it, or leave it out and the file goes to your system's default screenshot folder.

before: Give it a screen. Get the states people hit first: empty, loading, error, offline, no results and success.
after: Most screens are built for the best case: lots of data, fast network, nothing breaking. Real people hit the other cases first. This skill takes a screen you are building and finds those states, then builds each one properly.

before: Give it a screenshot. Get phone numbers, emails, keys and IDs masked on your own computer before you share it.
after: A copy of your screenshot with phone numbers, emails, API keys and ID numbers covered, ready to share or paste into a chat. The work happens on your own computer, so the original image is never uploaded anywhere.

before: Give it a screenshot or mockup. Get matching UI built with your own parts, compared side by side with the image.
after: A working screen that matches your screenshot or mockup, built from your project's own components and colours, then compared against the image and corrected. Pictures usually go wrong in the same ways: spacing close but off, text sizes guessed, colours picked by eye, a missing state.

before: Describe the site. Get a scroll-driven page with layered depth, motion and smooth reveals, built in code.
after: Describe the site. Get a scroll-driven page with layered depth, motion and smooth reveals, built in code. Bring a brief for the site. Use the result to plan your next step.

before: Give a topic and target keyword. Get a long post with an answer first, FAQs and internal links.
after: A finished long post of 800 to 3,000 words built to rank in search and to be quoted by AI answer tools. It opens with a two or three sentence direct answer, then an introduction that names your keyword early, then a fixed set of sections.

before: Give it your site, folder or Search Console export. Get why pages are not indexed and a fix list.
after: A diagnosis of why Google is skipping your pages, with a fix list and a cleaner site plan. It finds what is behind messages like "Discovered but not currently indexed" and says whether each cause is content, technical or structure.

before: Give it your topic. Get keywords sorted by search intent, grouped into themes and ranked for what to write first.
after: A keyword list sorted by what searchers want, grouped into topics and ranked by what to write first. It works with any keyword tool, or with Search Console data alone if you have none.

before: Give it a keyword and the pages that rank. Get a brief with search intent, gaps to fill, and an outline.
after: A writer-ready brief for one page, built from what the top-ranking pages actually say. You give a keyword and three to five results that rank.

before: Give it last season sales. Get how much to buy early, how much to hold back, and when to mark down.
after: A season buy plan that says how much to order up front, how much to keep in reserve, and when to mark items down. It balances two costs: running out of winners and being stuck with leftovers.

before: Give it two seawater measures like alkalinity and pH. Get the full carbonate chemistry worked out.
after: Give it two seawater measures like alkalinity and pH. Get the full carbonate chemistry worked out. Bring two measured carbonate variables with units. Use the result to plan your next step.

before: Give it a plan or change you feel sure about. Get a fresh reviewer's hardest objections, sorted by what matters.
after: A set of the hardest objections to a plan or change you feel sure about, sorted by how much each one matters. In a long session, guesses quietly turn into facts.

before: Point it at your project. Get leaked keys found, env files tidied and a plan to rotate secrets.
after: A scan of your project for leaked keys and passwords, plus a clear order for fixing them. It finds likely credentials in the working files and ranks each one critical, high or lower, so you start with what could hurt most.

before: Name your pipeline and secret store. Get a safe plan for storing, reading and rotating secrets.
after: A safe plan for how your pipeline stores, reads and changes secrets, without printing a single value. You name the secrets, who owns them, what uses them and which store you have, such as Vault, a cloud secret manager or GitHub Actions.

before: Name an industry. Get a report on its size, main players, competition and trends.
after: An industry report showing how big the sector is, who the main players are, how they compete and where it is heading. This version is set up for Indian markets.

before: Give it your project. Get a scan for code flaws, weak packages and exposed secrets, with fixes ranked.
after: A security scan of your project that finds code flaws, risky packages and exposed secrets, with fixes ranked by severity. Three bundled Python tools do the work and can export JSON for your build pipeline.

before: Give it a pull request or commit. Get a security review of only what changed, with risks ranked.
after: Give it a pull request or commit. Get a security review of only what changed, with risks ranked. Bring a pull request, commit range or diff. Use the result to plan your next step.

before: Give it a security alert. Get severity, who to tell, what to preserve and the next steps.
after: Give it a security alert. Get severity, who to tell, what to preserve and the next steps. Bring the alert or event details, in JSON if you have them. Use the result to plan your next step.

before: Describe your system. Get a scoped review of code, servers, sign-in and daily operations.
after: A scoped security audit of your web app, API or cloud setup, with each issue rated, mapped to a known standard and paired with a fix.

before: Describe your setup and size. Get which CIS safeguards you need first, your gaps and a fix order.
after: A short list of CIS safeguards your organisation should do first, the gaps you have today, and the order to close them. It starts with the one decision that matters most: which of three Implementation Groups you belong to.

before: Give it a text, example or diagram. Get questions that make students explain the why behind each step.
after: Questions placed at the right points in your learning material so students stop to explain why each step is true, not just what it says.

before: Give it a site or page. Get a scored SEO report and ranked fixes. Collects data from websites.
after: A scored SEO report on your site or page, plus an action plan with the fixes in priority order. Say "perform seo analysis on" and a URL, and it runs a full audit and saves two files: a detailed findings report and a ranked action plan.

before: Save your site's SEO state today. Get a warning when rankings, tags or pages slip later.

before: Name what you want to set up. Get one small step at a time, with the steps left shown.

after: A weekly schedule, a shift pattern and a fair rotation for the shifts nobody likes, ready to hand to your team. Fair rotation cuts complaints and swap requests.

after: A clear go or no-go before you push code live, with the blockers listed so you know what to fix first. It catches the problems that usually show up after launch.

after: A short set of documents that lets a reviewer judge an AI-built app without guessing what it was meant to do. AI writes code fast but leaves no record of intent, so nobody can tell if the app is safe to ship.

before: Describe a late, lost or damaged shipment. Get the right steps, claim paperwork and carrier messages.
after: A plan for a late, lost or damaged shipment, with the claim paperwork and carrier messages ready to send. Acting fast and documenting well decides whether you get paid.

after: A SQL query that has been written, tested or sped up, or a database migration ready to run. Describe the data you need in plain words.

before: Get staff accounts with old logins, inactive status or too much access, so your store stays safe.
after: A report on which Shopify staff accounts are a risk to your store. It lists accounts with no login for a set number of days (90 by default), accounts marked inactive but still set up, and accounts with full or owner-level access.

before: Say what is changing. Get a clear internal announcement, a rollout plan and answers to likely questions.
after: A clear internal announcement, a plan for sending it and answers to the questions people will ask. Tell it what is changing and who it affects.

before: Give it a training goal. Get a session plan for teachers that uses adult learning methods.
after: A teacher training session plan built on how adults actually learn. Give it the topic, who is attending and how long you have. The skill draws on research on effective teacher development, including work by Timperley, Darling-Hammond and Desimone.

before: List the people affected by your project. Get a power and interest grid with how to talk to each group.
after: A grid of who matters to your project and exactly how to talk to each group. List the people and groups affected, or share an org chart or brief and let the skill infer them.

before: Give it a startup loan offer. Get the cost, warrants and covenants explained, with points to question.

before: Point it at a Vercel app. Get cost and speed problems found from real production metrics, with fixes.
after: A list of what is costing you money or slowing your Vercel app, found from real production numbers instead of guesses, with a fix for each.

before: Say "deploy my app". Get it live on Vercel and a link you can share.
after: Tell it to deploy and your app goes live on Vercel with a link to share. It makes a preview first, so you check before anything reaches real visitors.

before: Say "deploy my app". Get it live on Vercel as a preview or production site, with the link.
after: Say deploy my app and get a live address back. It uses the Vercel command line tool if you have it, and a no-login fallback if you do not.

before: Describe the change. Get code grounded in your real files, with each step checked before it counts.
after: Code that matches what is actually in your project: no made-up functions, no guessed imports, no placeholders. Each step is checked before it counts as done.

before: Point it at your repo. Get release numbers and a changelog worked out from your commits.
after: Point it at your repo. Get release numbers and a changelog worked out from your commits. Bring a git repository with commit history. Use the result to plan your next step.

before: Point it at a fast-built app. Get dead code and broken imports removed without breaking routes or APIs.
after: An app built fast with AI, tidied up without breaking it. Dead imports, unused files and broken references are removed, while your routes, APIs, login and database stay exactly as they were.

before: Give it your channel goal. Get a video plan, scripts and ways to turn one long video into short clips.
after: A video plan you can start this week: what to make, for whom, and how to get several clips out of each long video. The skill first asks about your goal, audience, team size and what you already have, such as blog posts, webinars or demos.

before: Give it a video or podcast. Get versions in other languages that keep each speaker's voice, ready to correct.
after: Your video or podcast in new languages, still in each speaker's own voice, with a chance to fix the words before the final version. The skill uses the ElevenLabs dubbing service.

before: Describe your video. Get the right way to make it chosen first: generate, compose, or edit your footage.
after: Describe your video. Get the right way to make it chosen first: generate, compose, or edit your footage. Bring a description of the video you want. Use the result to plan your next step.

before: Describe how you handle Vietnamese personal data. Get your duties, transfer checks and a plan under the new law.
after: A clear list of what Vietnam's new personal data law asks of you, with gaps marked and a plan to close them. It matters because the law took effect on 1 January 2026 and reaches foreign firms that handle data about people in Vietnam.

before: Get your top customers by lifetime spend as a VIP list. It tags them in Shopify only if you ask.
after: A list of your best Shopify customers, ranked by what they have spent over time. You can use it to build a loyalty group, give them faster support or offer early access to new products.

before: Give it a clothing flat lay and a pose photo. Get a model-wearing shot. Your image model draws it, not Claude.
after: A photo of a model wearing your garment, made from a flat product shot and a pose photo. You skip the model, the studio and the shoot day.

before: Name a virus and a region. Get current lineages, weekly sequence shares and mutation frequencies from public data.
after: A plain summary of which virus lineages are showing up in public sequence data for a region, week by week. It is built for questions like what is circulating now, and it will not answer from memory or old examples.

before: Give it your site visit records and contact list. Get anonymous visits linked to known contacts, with unclear links flagged.
after: Anonymous website visits tied to the real contacts they belong to, with doubtful matches flagged instead of guessed. You can then see which channels brought in people you already know.

before: Give it a web page or screen. Get fixes for spacing, color, type and depth so it looks professional.
after: A web page or app screen that looks professional because the eye knows where to go first. You get a short list of fixes you can apply in code or in a design tool.

before: Name your model and GPU. Get a fast model server running, with settings for speed and memory.
after: A running model server that answers requests fast, with settings picked to fit your GPU and model size. It speaks the same API as OpenAI, so your existing code points at it with a one-line change.

before: Name the concept. Get a lesson that shows it, names it and checks it, using real objects.
after: A short lesson plan that teaches a new word or idea with real objects, in three clear moves: show it, name it, then check it.

after: The words in your text, sorted into everyday words, school words and subject words, so you know what to teach first. It saves you from pre-teaching the whole page.

after: A voice and tone guide anyone can use, from a new writer to an AI assistant. It tells people how your brand sounds and how that shifts from a sales page to an apology email.

after: Say what your voice assistant should do. Get a working agent that talks with customers, with tools and a web embed. Bring what the assistant should do and say. Use the result to plan your next step.

after: A ranked list of automation options for your warehouse, with cost, payback time and risks for each, so you spend only where it pays off.

after: An answer to how many warehouses you need and where they should go. It balances shipping cost, delivery speed and the cost of running each site.

after: A plan for which product goes in which storage spot, so fast sellers sit close and slow ones sit far away. That cuts the distance pickers walk each day.

before: Give it your warehouses and demand. Get how much stock to hold at each level of your network.
after: A plan for how much stock to hold at every level of your network, from the central warehouse down to local sites. It keeps service high without tying up cash in extra stock.

after: A full plan for one WeChat Official Account article, built around how the platform works. Distribution is closed, sharing happens in Moments and readers tap titles that promise something.

before: Describe your business. Get a WhatsApp setup with broadcasts, automatic replies and support flows.

before: Run it on open orders. Get shipped orders with stale tracking and late unshipped ones, before customers ask.
after: A list of the orders most likely to trigger a "where is my order?" email, found before the email arrives. You can message those customers first.

before: Give it an audio file. Get a written transcript in 99 languages, or an English translation.
after: Give it an audio file. Get a written transcript in 99 languages, or an English translation. Bring an audio or video file. Use the result to plan your next step.

before: Give it your new leads. Get them ranked by fit and urgency, with talking points and follow-up drafts.
after: A ranked call list for today, taken from the new leads sitting in your HubSpot. You know who to ring first, what to say and what to send to the rest.

before: Give it a history source. Get a lesson series that teaches learners to ask who wrote it, when and why.
after: A lesson series that trains students to ask who wrote a source, when and why before they read a word. It builds the habit expert historians use, instead of treating each document as plain fact.

before: Run it on your store. Get your B2B companies with locations, catalogs and payment terms in one view.
after: A single view of every wholesale customer in your Shopify store: companies, their locations, price lists and payment terms. You stop clicking through admin pages one account at a time.

before: Give it your content. Get why and how questions that push learners past memorising to understanding.
after: A set of why and how questions that make learners explain what they study instead of repeating it. Asking "why is this true?" forces connections to what they already know, and that is what helps memory.

before: Say what people tried before and why it failed. Get a named new method and the reason it works now.
after: The story that explains why your offer works when other things people tried did not. You get a named method with a believable reason behind it, ready to use in copy.

before: Describe your product. Get a pricing survey, plan tiers and a price built on what buyers will actually pay.
after: A price and plan structure built on what buyers say they will pay, set while your product is still changeable. Most new products miss revenue targets because price came last.

before: Tell it what you sell. Get two survey questions to send customers and a way to turn answers into a best price.
after: Two short surveys that give you a best price from real customer answers, plus the steps to turn those answers into a number. It replaces guessing and asking "how much would you pay?", which overstates by about half.

before: Ask why you win and lose. Get patterns from closed deals: loss stage, common objections and deal traits.
after: The patterns behind your closed deals: where you lose, what buyers object to and what wins have in common. A leader can act on this instead of trusting hunches from the last painful loss.

after: A new Windows desktop app, set up and built the way Microsoft recommends for WinUI 3. You describe what the app should do and get a working project instead of a blank folder and a long setup guide.

after: Screen layouts you can read, share and build from, at three levels of detail. You see where everything goes before anyone spends time on visual design.

after: A system-level wireless simulation of your nodes and traffic, with throughput results you can compare. You see how the network behaves under load before building anything.

after: A review pass that catches the mistakes AI makes in WooCommerce code before they reach a live store. These errors can lose orders or open a security hole where money is involved.

after: Ideas that make people talk about your product, each checked against six reasons things spread. You see which parts of your idea are likely to be shared and which are weak.

after: A plan for a diagram or visual that sits beside your words so the idea sticks. People remember explanations better when they get both a verbal and a visual version.

after: A full blog post built for search and ready to paste into WordPress. You give a keyword and get a long, structured article with the extras that usually take another hour.
